item.title: LIVE! UFC Vegas 123 Results: Moicano vs. Nolan
item.description: Renato Moicano and Tom Nolan clash in UFC Vegas 123 main event. | ﻿Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC MMA Fighting has UFC Vegas 123 results for the Moicano vs. Nolan fight card, a live blog of the main event, and more from Meta APEX in Las Vegas on Saturday night. In the main event, Renato Moicano squares off against Tom Nolan in a lightweight contest. Moicano recently got back in the win column with a second-round face-crank submission win over Chris Duncan, while Nolan has rebounded from a loss in his UFC debut with five straight victories. Randy Brown faces short-notice replacement Jacobe Smith in a welterweight contest in the co-main event. Check out UFC Vegas 123 results below. Main Card (Paramount+, 8 p.m.) Renato Moicano vs. Tom Nolan Randy Brown vs. Jacobe Smith Ode Osbourne vs. Cody Durden Yana Santos vs. Luana Santos Jean-Paul Lebosnoyani vs. Farman Hasanov Preliminary Card (Paramount+, 5 p.m.) Francis Marshall vs. Dakota Hope Rodrigo Sezinando vs. Theodor Berggren Julian Erosa vs. Jeong Yeong Lee Zachary Reese vs. Mickey Gall Joe Kropschot def. Nick Klein via submission (armbar) at 1:25, R2 Piera Rodriguez def. Talita Alencar via unanimous decision (30-27. 30-27, 30-27) Lucia Szabova def. Tainara Lisboa via TKO (ground strikes) at 3:20, R3

item.title: Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian Mbilli LIVE round-by-round updates
item.description: Canelo Alvarez and Christian Mbilli clash for WBC title Saturday. | AFP via Getty Images MMA Fighting has Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian Mbilli live round-by-round updates for one of the most anticipated boxing fights of the year at the Kingdom Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Saturday. The main event is expected to begin around 5:30 p.m. ET on DAZN pay-per-view . Check out our Canelo vs. Mbilli results page to find out what happened on the undercard. Canelo Alvarez (63-3-2, 39 knockouts) is trying to bounce back after a unanimous decision loss to Bud Crawford, costing him his WBC, IBF, WBO, and The Ring super middleweight titles. Christian Mbilli (29-0-1, 24 knockouts) was elevated to the WBC super middleweight champion after Bud Crawford retired. Mbilli recorded a split draw against Lester Martinez last September. Get the Canelo vs. Mbilli round-by-round live blog below: That’s it for the undercard, the legendary Canelo takes on the undefeated Mbilli next. Out first, the champion, Christian Mbilli. Here comes Canelo, aiming to have gold around his waist again. Hector Afu the third man in the ring for tonight’s main event. Round 1: Lots of movement from both men as they angle to take control of the center of the ring. Mbilli flicking out jabs, Canelo nearly catches him with a counter right. Canelo dodges out of the way of a body shot. He doubles up on the jab, neither fighter landing anything of note yet. There’s a counter jab by Canelo that scores. Mbilli lands a left to the body, referee warns him of a potential low blow. Jab from Mbilli. Better jab from Canelo. Mbilli with pressure in the corner, Canelo defending well. Mbilli upping the volume, this is his path to victory even if he’s catching a lot of arm and glove. Not much to score there, slight edge to the challenger. MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Canelo. Round 2: Canelo patiently jabbing at Mbilli’s defense. Mbilli with a lot of side-to-side movement. Can he keep that pace for another 11 rounds? Left hook by Canelo sets up a straight right. Mbilli answers with a jab and a few straight punches. Right hook from Canelo gets around Mbilli’s guard. Mbilli answers with a flurry, not sure how much is scoring. Canelo hits the body and dodges away from a counter. Mbilli pressing forward to close out the round, he lands a right, but eats a body shot. Good right from Mbilli before the round ends. MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Canelo. Overall, 20-18 Canelo. Round 3: Mbilli starting quick with jabs to the body. Close exchange as both fighters show good defense. Canelo hits the body, Mbilli’s counters are wide. More corner pressure from Mbilli. Canelo rips the body. Mbilli is busy, he could be winning over the judges with sheer activity. Canelo waves Mbilli on, dropping the gloves as he dares Mbilli to come forward. Both fighters miss with big punches. Short uppercut by Canelo. MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Mbilli. Overall, 29-28 Canelo. Round 4: Mbilli doing good work when he has Can

item.title: Ebola scare in Adamawa: NCDC confirms negative tests
item.description: …Two suspected cases test negative after two rounds of laboratory tests By Chioma Obinna The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) last night said two suspected Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) cases in Adamawa State tested negative after two rounds of laboratory tests, assuring Nigerians that the confirmed case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) remains the only confirmed infection reported in the country. The agency said the two individuals, who presented with symptoms suggestive of Ebola in Yola, were isolated as public health authorities commenced investigations and appropriate response measures. In a press statement yesterday, the Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, said the report was received by the Adamawa State Public Health Emergency Operations Centre (PHEOC) in the early hours of October 30, 2026. He said samples collected from the individuals were subjected to laboratory testing to establish the cause of their illness, adding that both tested negative for Ebola after two rounds of testing. “Fortunately, the samples turned out negative for EBV after two rounds of testing,” Idris said. He clarified that there was currently no laboratory-confirmed Ebola case in Adamawa, stressing that the index case previously confirmed in the FCT remained the only confirmed case in Nigeria. “At this juncture, I wish to commend the efforts of the Adamawa State’s Commissioner for Health and his team for their proactive approach. NCDC will continue to provide appropriate technical support to the Adamawa State Government to strengthen their response operations,” he said. The latest development comes amid heightened public health vigilance following the confirmation of a Bundibugyo Ebola case in Abuja involving a traveller who arrived in Nigeria from Uganda. The emergence of the suspected cases in Adamawa had raised concerns about a possible spread of the disease, prompting the state and federal health authorities to activate investigation and precautionary measures. However, the negative laboratory results have ruled out Ebola infection in the two individuals, based on the tests reported by the NCDC. Idris urged Nigerians to remain calm and refrain from circulating unverified information or speculation about the situation. “We urge members of the public to remain calm and avoid sharing unverified information or speculation about the situation. The public is encouraged to obtain information from official government and public health communication channels,” he said. The NCDC director-general, however, emphasised the need for continued vigilance, noting that Ebola was a serious infectious disease requiring prompt identification, appropriate clinical management and effective infection prevention and control measures. item.content:encoded: …Two suspected cases test negative after two rounds of laboratory tests By Chioma Obinna The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) last night said two suspected Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) cases in Adamawa State tested negative after two rounds of laboratory tests, assuring Nigerians that the confirmed case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) remains the only confirmed infection reported in the country. The agency said the two individuals, who presented with symptoms suggestive of Ebola in Yola, were isolated as public health authorities commenced investigations and appropriate response measures. In a press statement yesterday, the Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, said the report was received by the Adamawa State Public Health Emergency Operations Centre (PHEOC) in the early hours of October 30, 2026. He said samples collected from the individuals were subjected to laboratory testing to establish the cause of their illness, adding that both tested negative for Ebola after two rounds of testing. “Fortunately, the samples turned out negative for EBV after two rounds of testing,” Idris said. He clarified that there was currently no laboratory-confirmed Ebola case in Adamawa, stressing that the index case previously confirmed in the FCT remained the only confirmed case in Nigeria. “At this juncture, I wish to commend the efforts of the Adamawa State’s Commissioner for Health and his team for their proactive approach. NCDC will continue to provide appropriate technical support to the Adamawa State Government to strengthen their response operations,” he said. The latest development comes amid heightened public health vigilance following the confirmation of a Bundibugyo Ebola case in Abuja involving a traveller who arrived in Nigeria from Uganda. The emergence of the suspected cases in Adamawa had raised concerns about a possible spread of the disease, prompting the state and federal health authorities to activate investigation and precautionary measures. However, the negative laboratory results have ruled out Ebola infection in the two individuals, based on the tests reported by the NCDC. Idris urged Nigerians to remain calm and refrain from circulating unverified information or speculation about the situation. “We urge members of the public to remain calm and avoid sharing unverified information or speculation about the situation. The public is encouraged to obtain information from official government and public health communication channels,” he said. The NCDC director-general, however, emphasised the need for continued vigilance, noting that Ebola was a serious infectious disease requiring prompt identification, appropriate clinical management and effective infection prevention and control measures. He advised anyone experiencing symptoms such as fever, severe weakness, headache, muscle pain, vomiting, diarrhoea or unexplained bleeding, particularly after a relevant exposure, to seek immediate medical attention and disclose any relevant travel or contact history to healthcare workers. “Individuals should avoid self-medication and follow the advice of healthcare professionals,” he said. Idris said the NCDC, in collaboration with the Adamawa State Government and other relevant stakeholders, would continue to monitor the situation and provide updates as verified information became available. He added that Nigeria’s public health authorities remained committed to protecting the population through early detection, evidence-based public health action, transparent communication and a coordinated national response. The post Ebola scare in Adamawa: NCDC confirms negative tests appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Benvenuto Cellini salvages Breeders' Cup turf races for Europeans
item.description: Bacio, ridden by Juan Hernandez, wins the Breeders Cup Turf Sprint during the 43rd running of the Breeders' Cup Championships at Keeneland racetrack in Lexington, Ky., on Saturday. Photo by Mark Abraham/UPI LEXINGTON, Ky., Oct. 31 (UPI) -- Just when it looked like a powerful European contingent would be shut out of Saturday's Breeders' Cup turf races at Keeneland, along came Benvenuto Cellini to lead a cavalry charge of foreigners home in the big one, the $5 million Turf. Euros had dominated Friday's juvenile turf eventsm but Americans looked like at least evening the score Saturday as older horses took center stage. Benvenuto Cellini, a Frankel colt trained by Aidan O'Brien and ridden by Ryan Moore, put paid to that. Rallying from far back in the 1 1/2-mile Turf, he reached contention by mid-stretch, found room between rivals and ran through to win by 3/4 length. He was followed home by Map of Stars, Diamond Necklace, Tiffany and Survie, all veterans of European campaigns. Owned by Peter Brant and Ireland's Coolmore partners, Benvenuto Cellini made his mark with a victory in the Group 1 Irish Derby on July 28, but was winless in three starts since. He finished ninth in the Group 1 Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe on Oct. 4. And now he could be headed to Hong Kong for December's international races. Horses in the Breeders Cup Turf Spring pass the foliage during the 43rd running of the Breeders' Cup Championships at Keeneland racetrack in Lexington, Ky., on Saturday. Photo by Mark Abraham/UPI O'Brien, who also trains Diamond Necklace, won his 24th Breeders' Cup race, moving him two ahead of Bob Baffert. The two entered the weekend competition tied with 21 wins each. O'Brien won two on Friday while Baffert got one. Earlier in the day on the firm Keeneland greensward: $2 million Mile Deterministic shot to a big lead in the stretch run of the Mile, and then was all out to survive a late bid by the favorite and defending champion Notable Speech. A 5-year-old son of 2015 Breeders' Cup Dirt Mile winner Liam's Map, Deterministic looked like a sure winner as he showed the way into the final furlong with Notable Speech still far behind. Jockey Kendrick Carmouche kept after the winner as William Buick brought Notable Speech quickly around the rest of the field and into contention. The Godolphin standard bearer was still gaining as Deterministic hit the finish 3/4 length in front, finishing in 1:34.52. While the result was a significant rebuff of a strong European contingent at this year's Breeders' Cup, it was a lonely one, as the invaders finished second and third behind the top two. Deterministic finished second to Notable Speech in their last race, the Grade 1 Woodbine Mile, on Sept. 12. Before that, he had six straight wins for trainer Miguel Clement and an ownership combine headed by St. Elias Stables. item.content:encoded: Bacio, ridden by Juan Hernandez, wins the Breeders Cup Turf Sprint during the 43rd running of the Breeders' Cup Championships at Keeneland racetrack in Lexington, Ky., on Saturday. Photo by Mark Abraham/UPI LEXINGTON, Ky., Oct. 31 (UPI) -- Just when it looked like a powerful European contingent would be shut out of Saturday's Breeders' Cup turf races at Keeneland, along came Benvenuto Cellini to lead a cavalry charge of foreigners home in the big one, the $5 million Turf. Euros had dominated Friday's juvenile turf eventsm but Americans looked like at least evening the score Saturday as older horses took center stage. Benvenuto Cellini, a Frankel colt trained by Aidan O'Brien and ridden by Ryan Moore, put paid to that. Rallying from far back in the 1 1/2-mile Turf, he reached contention by mid-stretch, found room between rivals and ran through to win by 3/4 length. He was followed home by Map of Stars, Diamond Necklace, Tiffany and Survie, all veterans of European campaigns. Owned by Peter Brant and Ireland's Coolmore partners, Benvenuto Cellini made his mark with a victory in the Group 1 Irish Derby on July 28, but was winless in three starts since. He finished ninth in the Group 1 Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe on Oct. 4. And now he could be headed to Hong Kong for December's international races. Horses in the Breeders Cup Turf Spring pass the foliage during the 43rd running of the Breeders' Cup Championships at Keeneland racetrack in Lexington, Ky., on Saturday. Photo by Mark Abraham/UPI O'Brien, who also trains Diamond Necklace, won his 24th Breeders' Cup race, moving him two ahead of Bob Baffert. The two entered the weekend competition tied with 21 wins each. O'Brien won two on Friday while Baffert got one. Earlier in the day on the firm Keeneland greensward: $2 million Mile Deterministic shot to a big lead in the stretch run of the Mile, and then was all out to survive a late bid by the favorite and defending champion Notable Speech. A 5-year-old son of 2015 Breeders' Cup Dirt Mile winner Liam's Map, Deterministic looked like a sure winner as he showed the way into the final furlong with Notable Speech still far behind. Jockey Kendrick Carmouche kept after the winner as William Buick brought Notable Speech quickly around the rest of the field and into contention. The Godolphin standard bearer was still gaining as Deterministic hit the finish 3/4 length in front, finishing in 1:34.52. While the result was a significant rebuff of a strong European contingent at this year's Breeders' Cup, it was a lonely one, as the invaders finished second and third behind the top two. Deterministic finished second to Notable Speech in their last race, the Grade 1 Woodbine Mile, on Sept. 12. Before that, he had six straight wins for trainer Miguel Clement and an ownership combine headed by St. Elias Stables. "If anything, I think we were a bit unlucky in the Woodbine race," said Clement, who won his first Breeders' Cup race. "This was a more truly run race with a full field." The Woodbine Mile had a field of six, and Deterministic was alone on the lead before surrendering late. $2 million Filly & Mare Turf While American runners took the worst of it in Friday's Breeders' Cup 2-year-old races, Kathynmarissa added to Deterministic's victory in turning the tide Saturday with a stretch-running score in the Filly & Mare Turf. It was a gutsy effort, but perhaps aided in part by unlucky post position draws by the visitors. Kathynmarissa, a 5-year-old American Pharoah mare trained by Chad Brown, won the 1 3/16-mile heat by 3/4 length over Gimme a Nother, a South African-bred mare now trained in the U.S. by Graham Motion. The two star Euros, Precise and Blue Bolt, finished third and fourth -- a significant achievement after starting from gates No. 11 and 12, respectively. Kathynmarissa has been a force in the division since her debut in spring 2024 and entered the Breeders' Cup after winning four of her previous five starts, including the Grade 1 Diana at Saratoga this summer over yielding turf. Gimme a Nother has been a revelation for Motion, winning her last four starts. It appeared at the sixteenth pole she might make it five in a row only to run out of steam in the final yards. "Yeah, they defeated us yesterday on our home turf," Brown said in reference to the European dominance in Friday's 2-year-old turf races. "But I just had a feeling about today." $1 Million Turf Sprint Bacio, trained by Kentucky-based Wesley Ward, handily dispatched a field that included some of Europe's best to win the 5 1/2-furlong Turf Sprint by 2 lengths. The 3-year-old Maclean's Music colt, however, can't be pigeonholed as an American as his last two starts, both victories, came in the Palace of Holyroodhouse Handicap at Royal Ascot and the Group 1 Norfolk Stakes at York in the north of England. Earlier, he won three of four starts at four different American tracks. With Juan Hernandez up, Bacio battled early with Miss Yechance, last seen winning the Group 1 Prix de l'Abbaye de Longchamp. He put her away and then held off last year's winner, California-based Cy Fair, and another European, Starlust, who finished close together in second and third, respectively.

item.title: Barca hammer Alaves 6-1 to retain Liga top spot
item.description: Raphinha and Lamine Yamal struck twice each as Barcelona thrashed Alaves 6-1 on Saturday to reclaim their La Liga lead and get back on track after two damaging defeats. Earlier Atletico Madrid, second, earned a solid 2-0 win at Levante, but Barca moved back two points clear of the Rojiblancos by routing the Basque visitors at Camp Nou. Still stinging after a Champions League defeat by Paris Saint-Germain and then last weekend’s La Liga home Clasico loss against rivals Real Madrid, Hansi Flick’s side found their groove once more. Raphinha netted twice in the first half, either side of a Fermin Lopez strike, and Yamal found the net just before the interval. Teenage winger Yamal netted again midway through the second half and substitute Anthony Gordon chipped home Barca’s sixth, before Mariano Diaz pulled one back for Alaves. There was a minute’s silence at the start of each of the day’s matches in memory of the 69 victims of the train crash in the province of Toledo that rocked Spain this week. Flick lined up with Dutch midfielder Frenkie de Jong playing at centre-back and youngster Brian Farinas making his first start at right-back, amid a spate of defensive injuries. It did not hamper the champions. Barcelona moved ahead in the eighth minute, with La Liga’s top scorer Raphinha continuing his red-hot form. Midfield maestro Pedri played in Lopez, who pulled the ball across for the Brazil international to bundle home. Alaves came close through Abde Rebbach before Lopez doubled Barcelona’s lead in the 23rd minute. Yamal slipped the midfielder in and, from a tight angle, Lopez smashed the ball across goal and fortuitously in at the far post, seemingly intending to cross it. Karim Adeyemi and Yamal both missed glorious chances from close range to expand on Barca’s lead, with Raphinha showing the duo how to do it as he bagged his 15th league goal. Lopez sent the forward through on goal and Raphinha produced a lethal finish across Antonio Sivera. Perhaps frustrated by his miss, Yamal smashed home the fourth with an instinctive low strike from the edge of the box in first half stoppage time. Adeyemi blazed another presentable chance over the crossbar early in the second half after Lopez unselfishly set him up. Yamal got Barca’s fifth with a neat dink over the goalkeeper after substitute Gabriel Jesus played him through on goal. Gordon produced a similar finish for Barca’s sixth and the only tarnish on their evening was former Real Madrid striker Diaz netting late on. – Seven in a row – Earlier in Valencia Diego Simeone’s Atletico had temporarily climbed a point clear of the Catalan giants with goals from Alejandro Grimaldo and Giuliano Simeone against Levante. Atletico recorded a seventh consecutive league win to continue their strong form and put pressure on the reigning champions. “I’m very happy with the team’s work,” Atletico coach Simeone told Movistar. “We’re very far from the end of the season… we’ll keep going game by game.” Alex Baena, the visito

There was a minute’s silence at the start of each of the day’s matches in memory of the 69 victims of the train crash in the province of Toledo that rocked Spain this week. Flick lined up with Dutch midfielder Frenkie de Jong playing at centre-back and youngster Brian Farinas making his first start at right-back, amid a spate of defensive injuries. It did not hamper the champions. Barcelona moved ahead in the eighth minute, with La Liga’s top scorer Raphinha continuing his red-hot form. Midfield maestro Pedri played in Lopez, who pulled the ball across for the Brazil international to bundle home. Alaves came close through Abde Rebbach before Lopez doubled Barcelona’s lead in the 23rd minute. Yamal slipped the midfielder in and, from a tight angle, Lopez smashed the ball across goal and fortuitously in at the far post, seemingly intending to cross it. Karim Adeyemi and Yamal both missed glorious chances from close range to expand on Barca’s lead, with Raphinha showing the duo how to do it as he bagged his 15th league goal. Lopez sent the forward through on goal and Raphinha produced a lethal finish across Antonio Sivera. Perhaps frustrated by his miss, Yamal smashed home the fourth with an instinctive low strike from the edge of the box in first half stoppage time. Adeyemi blazed another presentable chance over the crossbar early in the second half after Lopez unselfishly set him up. Yamal got Barca’s fifth with a neat dink over the goalkeeper after substitute Gabriel Jesus played him through on goal. Gordon produced a similar finish for Barca’s sixth and the only tarnish on their evening was former Real Madrid striker Diaz netting late on. – Seven in a row – Earlier in Valencia Diego Simeone’s Atletico had temporarily climbed a point clear of the Catalan giants with goals from Alejandro Grimaldo and Giuliano Simeone against Levante. Atletico recorded a seventh consecutive league win to continue their strong form and put pressure on the reigning champions. “I’m very happy with the team’s work,” Atletico coach Simeone told Movistar. “We’re very far from the end of the season… we’ll keep going game by game.” Alex Baena, the visitors’ main creative outlet, set up both goals as Simeone recorded his 344th La Liga win at the helm of Atletico, matching the club’s record set by Luis Aragones. “I don’t feel it much as mine, but it belongs to my players, everyone who has been with me for so many years,” said Simeone, who started coaching Atletico in 2011. Atletico host Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Tuesday before welcoming Barca to the Metropolitano stadium next weekend in La Liga. On Sunday, Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, third, visit Racing Santander among other fixtures. AFP The post Barca hammer Alaves 6-1 to retain Liga top spot appeared first on Vanguard News .

Jaime Munguia def. Nikita Zon by Unanimous Decision Immediate Reaction: Nearly a disastrous ending for Munguia, who nearly got stopped in the sixth round but showcased his resilience and ultimately did enough to win wide on the cards. Round 8: Hard left to the body lands for Munguia. Munguia lands a couple up top now. Zon looks to the body himself, targeting both sides. Clean counter right from Munguia picks off Zon. Zon lands one punch and dives in to clinch. Uppercut from Zon makes partial contact. Zon lands a counter left and Munguia wants to get it back but can’t find a home for the punches. Another clash of heads at the bell. I edge Zon, 75-77. Round 7: Munguia getting support from the crowd to start the round. Two body shots from Munguia land well. Two straight rights from Munguia score up top. Zon lands a jab and Munguia lands three punches in return. Zon lands a body shot that has Munguia back along the ropes for a moment. Zon having a hard time keeping pace and it’s allowing Munguia time to fight at a comfortable pace for himself. Munguia 10-9, 68-65. Round 6: Straight left hand from Zon makes partial contact. UPPERCUT FROM ZON STAGGERS MUNGUIA! Munguia getting rocked on the ropes and might be out on his feet! Munguia goes down but it’s ruled a push. Heavy shots from Zon have Munguia seemingly ready to go. Munguia lands a counter but is in desperate shape. Munguia starts landing as Zon punches himself out for the moment. Munguia lands a series of hard punches in a striking chance of momentum! Munguia somehow fought himself back into that round, but I’m edging it to Zon. Zon 10-9, 56-58. Round 5: Munguia comes out trying to come forward on Zon, having much less success fighting on the back foot. Left hand from Munguia lands up top. Zon throws a combination and lands a straight left at the end of it. Another left lands for Zon with Munguia in the corner. Hard right lands to the body that staggers Zon! Munguia tries to follow up but can’t find the follow up to put him down. Munguia 10-9, 49-46. Round 4: Munguia starts the round with a combination that ends downstairs to the body. Straight right from Munguia lands up top. Zon standing his ground and lands some shots sporadically. Two punches from Zon land as Munguia gets backed into a corner. Zon lands a hrd right hook up top. Both fighters exchanging shots and Munguia looks like he’s not taking these shots so well. Munguia lands a couple of clean shots down the stretch which edges the round towards him, for me. item.title: F1 Mexico GP: Lewis Hamilton beats George Russell and Charles Leclerc to pole
item.description: Motorsport photo Lewis Hamilton has earned Ferrari its first pole of the 2026 Formula 1 campaign by defeating George Russell in a thrilling qualifying shootout for the Mexico Grand Prix. Russell had taken provisional pole away from Charles Leclerc with his final run at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, but Hamilton responded with a marginally faster first sector to take pole by a minuscule 0.009s. As Hamilton delivered the Scuderia's first pole of the campaign and his own first pole for Ferrari, Leclerc could only find a slight improvement on his final tour as he conceded 0.119s to his Ferrari team-mate. Max Verstappen was fourth, just under two tenths behind, but will line up in fifth on Sunday. The Dutchman took a one-place grid penalty into qualifying for an on-track altercation with Liam Lawson during Friday practice. After a muted session championship leader Kimi Antonelli was fifth, with the top five was covered by just two tenths. In the shape of world champion Lando Norris , McLaren also looked like a threat for pole, but Norris wasn't able to nail his first flyer and then bailed out of his second. An irate Isack Hadjar was seventh for Red Bull after going off at the low-speed Turn 13, Red Bull's Achilles heel this weekend. Lawson was eighth but will move down to ninth for his share in the practice incident with Verstappen. That promoted his Racing Bulls team-mate Arvid Lindblad to eighth, while Lawson will line up on the fifth row alongside Alpine's Pierre Gasly . George Russell, Mercedes George Russell, Mercedes In Q2 Hamilton and Piastri were put under some pressure when they bailed out of their first flyers, needing a clean second effort to advance to Q3. While Hamilton booked a place in the top 10 shootout with fourth place in Q2, Piastri wasn't able to follow suit, with the Australian's horrid second sector, losing nearly half a second through the Esses due to a lack of rear grip, leaving him eliminated in 13th – nine-tenths of a second behind pacesetting team-mate Norris. Gasly narrowly made the cut in 10th at Audi's Nico Hulkenberg's expense. In the second Alpine Franco Colapinto managed to stay ahead of Piastri to take 12th, while Gabriel Bortoleto went out in 14th. Haas man Oliver Bearman wasn't able to string a clean lap together, losing his second flyer for track limits, and was dumped out in 15th with Carlos Sainz the only Williams in Q2 as he took 15th. The Q1 segment was red-flagged with 11 minutes on the clock for Fernando Alonso's stricken Aston Martin as the Spaniard ground to a halt at the Foro Sol arena with a power unit issue. It was a gut-wrenching exit for the two-time F1 world champion on what was looking like one of the team's most competitive circuits, with Alonso's only flyer almost good enough for Q2. Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing As Hamilton led the way with a 1m17.341s, Alonso's time didn't survive the test, with the Aston driver joined in the drop zone by Williams

George Russell, Mercedes George Russell, Mercedes In Q2 Hamilton and Piastri were put under some pressure when they bailed out of their first flyers, needing a clean second effort to advance to Q3. While Hamilton booked a place in the top 10 shootout with fourth place in Q2, Piastri wasn't able to follow suit, with the Australian's horrid second sector, losing nearly half a second through the Esses due to a lack of rear grip, leaving him eliminated in 13th – nine-tenths of a second behind pacesetting team-mate Norris. Gasly narrowly made the cut in 10th at Audi's Nico Hulkenberg's expense. In the second Alpine Franco Colapinto managed to stay ahead of Piastri to take 12th, while Gabriel Bortoleto went out in 14th. Haas man Oliver Bearman wasn't able to string a clean lap together, losing his second flyer for track limits, and was dumped out in 15th with Carlos Sainz the only Williams in Q2 as he took 15th. The Q1 segment was red-flagged with 11 minutes on the clock for Fernando Alonso's stricken Aston Martin as the Spaniard ground to a halt at the Foro Sol arena with a power unit issue. It was a gut-wrenching exit for the two-time F1 world champion on what was looking like one of the team's most competitive circuits, with Alonso's only flyer almost good enough for Q2. Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing As Hamilton led the way with a 1m17.341s, Alonso's time didn't survive the test, with the Aston driver joined in the drop zone by Williams driver Alex Albon , who was a tenth slower than his team-mate Sainz who did make the cut. Ryo Hirakawa was 19th on his grand prix debut, the 32-year-old Toyota WEC driver standings in for the benched Esteban Ocon at Haas. Ocon was dropped by the team without any further public explanation, though it is believed tensions between the driver and his team have hit a breaking point. Ocon has already been replaced by Ferrari junior Rafa Camara for 2027. Lance Stroll was 20th in the second Aston Martin, followed by Cadillac duo Sergio Perez and Valtteri Bottas . Bottas had already been due to start last anyway due to a grid penalty for taking a fifth Ferrari power unit. item.title: F1 grid: Starting positions for Mexican Grand Prix
item.description: Formula 1 returns to Mexico City this weekend for the Mexican Grand Prix - with Kimi Antonelli set to seal the world championship. The 20-year-old Italian holds a 123-point lead over Mercedes teammate George Russell and a 124-point advantage over Lewis Hamilton after his victory in Austin last time out. If Antonelli finishes ninth or higher in Mexico, he will be crowned world champion and, even if he doesn’t, Russell or Hamilton need to win the grand prix to extend the title race to Brazil. Antonelli cruised to victory from pole in Texas, with Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc in second and Red Bull’s Max Verstappen in third. Hamilton missed out on a podium, while an early penalty resulted in Russell finishing a lowly eighth. Lando Norris won last year’s race at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, on his way to his maiden world title. After missing out last year, Sergio Perez returns to his home race off the back of signing a new contract with Cadillac this week. item.title: Halloween Scare In Riyadh: Jaime Munguia Rises To Win
item.description: What To Know It took until the co-main event to deliver a thriller fitting of Halloween and Dia De Los Muertos in Riyadh on Saturday, thanks to Jaime Munguia and Daniel Zon. Munguia and Zon stole the show in a competitive contest with a Round of the Year candidate. Rafael Espinoza and Reito Tsutsumi weren’t in the ring long. Both should pursue a quick return in 2027. Jaime Munguia Gets A Scare From Nikita Zon Jaime Munguia of Tijuana, Mexico (47-2, 35 KOs) survived his first title defense against a tougher-than-expected Nikita Zon of Russia (12-1-1, 10 KOs), retaining his WBA World Super Middleweight title. That sentence makes it seem like an easy day at the office, doesn’t it? But it was far from the walkover fans expected from Munguia against a little-known opponent with no fights outside Russia against significant opposition. Through the first half, Munguia was on the brink of being stopped by the whirling dervish Zon. But Munguia bit down on the gumshield and pulled again to a decision win. Score were 117-111 twice, and 116-112. “I’m very happy . I’m very honored for this opportunity . Y eah, it was a little complicated . I t was kind of sticky there for a little bit, but I pulled it off, and that’s why it’s important, and it’s part of the growth,” said a relieved Munguia. Zon Came For More Than A Payday Zon didn’t come to lay down for a payday. It took Munguia a few rounds to get used to what he was seeing from the awkward-looking Russian. But when Munguia deciphered how to get to the body, he began gaining ground. At the end of round two, Zon caught Munguia with an uppercut, and Munguia had to cover up to the end of the round. Trainer Eddy Reynoso admonished Munguia. “He’s way too slow to be hitting you like that. You’ve got to focus!” The fight continued down a bumpy round, with both fighters trading shots and rounds on the card. READ MORE: Mexico vs the World Early Action: World 4, Mexico 1 Munguia vs Zon Round 6: Round of the Year Round six will go down as a 2026 Round of the Year nominee, something no one would have predicted with a 15-to-1 favorite in Munguia. Zon hurt Munguia with a wicked left uppercut, followed by right hooks. Munguia fired back using his offense as his defense. He rocked Zon, and both continued to trade, both emptying their reserves to stay in the fight. Veteran Nevada referee Tony Weeks was hovering nearby. He looked about to step in several times, but he kept his power dry. Weeks has taken heat for premature stoppages, most recently between Rolly Romero and Ismael Barroso . It must have been in his mind while watching Munguia and Zon. Zon was a whisker away from a second upset win over Munguia, following the knockout by Bruno Serace. Both men looked one hard shot away from getting wiped out. That kind of tension makes a fight exciting for fans. item.content:encoded: What To Know It took until the co-main event to deliver a thriller fitting of Halloween and Dia De Los Muertos in Riyadh on Saturday, thanks to Jaime Munguia and Daniel Zon. Munguia and Zon stole the show in a competitive contest with a Round of the Year candidate. Rafael Espinoza and Reito Tsutsumi weren’t in the ring long. Both should pursue a quick return in 2027. Jaime Munguia Gets A Scare From Nikita Zon Jaime Munguia of Tijuana, Mexico (47-2, 35 KOs) survived his first title defense against a tougher-than-expected Nikita Zon of Russia (12-1-1, 10 KOs), retaining his WBA World Super Middleweight title. That sentence makes it seem like an easy day at the office, doesn’t it? But it was far from the walkover fans expected from Munguia against a little-known opponent with no fights outside Russia against significant opposition. Through the first half, Munguia was on the brink of being stopped by the whirling dervish Zon. But Munguia bit down on the gumshield and pulled again to a decision win. Score were 117-111 twice, and 116-112. “I’m very happy . I’m very honored for this opportunity . Y eah, it was a little complicated . I t was kind of sticky there for a little bit, but I pulled it off, and that’s why it’s important, and it’s part of the growth,” said a relieved Munguia. Zon Came For More Than A Payday Zon didn’t come to lay down for a payday. It took Munguia a few rounds to get used to what he was seeing from the awkward-looking Russian. But when Munguia deciphered how to get to the body, he began gaining ground. At the end of round two, Zon caught Munguia with an uppercut, and Munguia had to cover up to the end of the round. Trainer Eddy Reynoso admonished Munguia. “He’s way too slow to be hitting you like that. You’ve got to focus!” The fight continued down a bumpy round, with both fighters trading shots and rounds on the card. READ MORE: Mexico vs the World Early Action: World 4, Mexico 1 Munguia vs Zon Round 6: Round of the Year Round six will go down as a 2026 Round of the Year nominee, something no one would have predicted with a 15-to-1 favorite in Munguia. Zon hurt Munguia with a wicked left uppercut, followed by right hooks. Munguia fired back using his offense as his defense. He rocked Zon, and both continued to trade, both emptying their reserves to stay in the fight. Veteran Nevada referee Tony Weeks was hovering nearby. He looked about to step in several times, but he kept his power dry. Weeks has taken heat for premature stoppages, most recently between Rolly Romero and Ismael Barroso . It must have been in his mind while watching Munguia and Zon. Zon was a whisker away from a second upset win over Munguia, following the knockout by Bruno Serace. Both men looked one hard shot away from getting wiped out. That kind of tension makes a fight exciting for fans. Later, Munguia described what happened from his perspective. “Well, he caught me, and then I caught him, and then I just got careless, and then he caught me again. “But that’s part of the process. That’s part of learning, and I just depended on the kind of work that I did, and that’s part of my growth,” said Munguia. Munguia made an impressive recovery between rounds. From there, Munguia buckled down and pulled away on the scorecards. He was still feeling some heat, but his hand wasn’t burning on the stove anymore. Munguia found one last chance to end the fight early with a body shot that hurt Zon, but it was near the end of the 11 th round, and he ran out of time. “I would give myself a six, seven out of 10. There were a few things that failed. There were a few things that I did not do, but I’m happy with my win, and I’m just going to go back and keep working,” said Munguia. Munguia Calls Out Martinez Zon, age 32, suffered his first defeat but won plenty of new fans and recognition for his performance. This is why underdogs who believe in their skills take these opportunities. He will get more opportunities from this loss than his anonymous wins in Russia. Munguia called out WBC World Super Middleweight champion Lester Martinez who was ringside in Riyadh, saying ‘you’re next my friend.’ It’s a fight sure to be a blockbuster in Southern California in 2027. Brief Return for Rafael Espinoza – Unification Ahead? It was a quick night for Rafael Espinoza, but at least fans got a song. Photo: Mark Robinson, Canelo Promotions After a year out of the ring, it was disappointing when Rafael Espinoza could only manage three rounds before his fight was stopped. The WBO World Featherweight champion Espinoza of Mexico (29-0, 25 KOs) faced a late replacement opponent, Ricardo Blandon of Nicaragua (21-7, 14 KOs). Like most of the 6-foot-1 champion’s opponents, Espinoza towered over Blandon. He showed no ring rust, with no concern about what was coming at him from Blandon. But Blandon was giving it his best. He was losing but he wasn’t being destroyed (at least not yet). In round three, Blandon suffered a cut over the left eye. It wasn’t a good situation, but we have all seen far worse cuts. The ringside physician, Dr. Neil Scott of the British Boxing Board of Control, wanted to take a look. With less than a minute left in the round in a championship fight, the physician told referee Janny Guzman to call off the fight at 2:22 of the round. Look at the cut. Would you have stopped the fight? If you were the ringside physician, would you stop the fight based on this cut suffered by Ricardo Blandon? Photo: Mark Robinson, Canelo Promotions It seemed too early to call off a fight at this level, with Blandon still holding his own in the fight and with no chance for the cutman to address the cut. Dr. Scott’s credentials are impeccable and he has experience at the highest level. It didn’t stop the armchair experts from complaining. With the anticipated move to featherweight by pound-for-pound great Naoya Inoue, the current featherweight champions are all waiting for the opportunity to face him. None want to risk losing in a unification fight before Inoue chooses his first opponent. It’s frustrating when featherweights should be working toward an undisputed champion. With lots of time between the end of the Espinoza fight and the start of the co-main event, boxing observers and the broadcast commentators criticized the champions including Bruce Carrington and Angelo Leo for not facing each other. Will Bruce Carrington and Rafael Espinoza step up to unify in 2027? And how about you, Abdullah Mason? Photo: Top Rank Boxing Carrington immediately protested on social media , saying he’s the only one in the division calling out opponents. “Don’t put me in a box with the rest of them. I been saying it BEFORE I even became champion and they was ducking because I was “too big of a risk.” LETS UNIFY” wrote Carrington. At least the fans got a song out of El Divino. Reito Tsutsumi Is For Real Reito Tsutsumi was disappointed with his performance despite winning by knockout. Photo: Mark Robinson, Canelo Promotions Featherweight prospect Reito Tsutsumi made his first scheduled ten-round appearance. Raymundo Rojas Garcia gave it a game try, but he was only good for two of those ten rounds. Tsutsumi of Osaka, Japan (6-0, 5 KOs) took it to Garcia of Mexico (16-3, 11 KOs) with an impressive display of his power, forcing the referee to step in at 2:22 of the second round. From the first hard left hook that landed 30 seconds into the fight, everyone watching knew where this fight was going. Tsutsumi has exceptionally broad, muscled shoulders, and he puts his full effort behind each punch. He’s as good a body puncher as anyone short of Naoya Inoue or Bam Rodriguez. Still, Tsutsumi was hard on himself after the fight. “Even though I could win and I’m very happy for the result, I just put too much strength into my fight. So, maybe next time I will do better,” he said through an interpreter, explaining he wants to focus on details beyond power. “Later, I will watch my own fight, and then I will s

item.title: Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian Mbilli live results, updates, highlights from 2026 boxing fight
item.description: Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian Mbilli live results, updates, highlights from 2026 boxing fight originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Saul 'Canelo' Alvarez attempts to reclaim a portion of the world super middleweight title when he returns to action on Halloween to challenge Christian Mbilli for the WBC's 168-pound belt. The fight is Canelo’s (63-3-2) second in Saudi Arabia, part of a deal with Riyadh Season. He last fought a year ago, where he lost his undisputed 12-stone title to fellow modern great Terence Crawford. Despite the time off, Canelo didn’t want to take an easy fight back. The multi-division champion aims to have gold around his waist again by beating the dangerous Mbilli. "I don’t believe in shortcuts. That’s why I go straight to the champion," Canelo said via Boxing Scene . "I already have that experience. I’ve been a champion many years, and I hope to be a champion again. I want to face the best, and he’s a champion, that’s it." Mbilli (29-0-1) has 23 knockout wins and took out Maciej Sulecki to become the interim champion. Promoted after Crawford relinquished the belt, his last fight was a draw. Mbilli is ready to prove he’s worthy of being champion against Canelo. "I’m ready to shock the world," said Mbilli. "I have a big respect for Canelo and all his career. I want to congratulate him for this, but Saturday will be a different story. I’m coming for the win." The Sporting News will provide analysis and highlights from the Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian Mbilli fight card and round-by-round coverage of the main event. He needs more of that. Now he scores upstairs. Now he bangs on the inside and takes Mbilli's return fire on his arms. Nice trading now and Alvarez lands a beauty of a left to the body. That punch couldn't have been more Mexican if you'd popped a sombrero on it. This is a Canelo round but Mbilli's relentless workrate over the final 30 seconds bodes well for the champ. SN unofficial scorecard: Mbilli 47-48 Canelo Round 4: Mbilli staying busy. His straight shots are backing Canelo up when they land, but he's smartly not engaging in any inside combat on the ropes. Canelo loads up the right uppercut, partially blocked. Mbilli gets back to work and now he lands nicely on the ropes. SN unofficial scorecard: Mbilli 38-38 Canelo Round 3: Mbilli loads up a little wildly and squares up. That feels like data Canelo will have downloaded for use a little later on. This is shaping into what we expected, with Canelo's accuracy set against Mbilli's volume. Now Alvarez tries to goad the champion in. He's not too keen to play ball. There's a lovely left to the midsection from Canelo, though. Mbilli smiles at the bell. Canelo scowls. That's a swing round. SN unofficial scorecard: Mbilli 28-29 Canelo Round 2: Mbilli straightens up his shots and has his best moments so far. Punches in bunches are the key to the champion. Canelo off target with a left hook before Mbilli puts everything into a right cross that whistles past Canelo's nose. A short right hand gets through, though. Canelo responds with a body shot. Good action, this is warming up nicely. SN unofficial scorecard: Mbilli 19-19 Canelo Round 1: They size each other up for the first minute before Canelo comes forward with a combination. Mbilli takes it on gloves and arms. Canelo has center ring and throws a left hook off the jab. Now Mbilli ships a jab coming in, his Mexican looking sharp early doors. Mbilli looks to attack the body; the referee tells him to keep them up. The champion tries to unload a couple of times before the bell. But Canelo has that all covered. SN unofficial scorecard: Mbilli 9-10 Canelo 5:56 p.m. ET - Just to add, I did not know I needed Buffer hollering in French in my life. But here we are, in big 2026. Allez le Buff! 5:54 p.m. ET - Michael Buffer has instructed us to get ready to rumble. After these introductions, we'll be going round-by-round. 5:46 p.m. ET - Here's Mbilli, looking relaxed and ready for business. Sure, Canelo is the A-side but the champion walking first is some real 21st-century nonsense, and you will not convince me otherwise. They're talking about Buster Douglas beating Mike Tyson on the DAZN broadcast. To be quite clear, this would not be that level of upset. Mbilli is an undefeated world champion and a world-class fighter in his own right. 5:42 p.m. ET - Okay then, main event time as the national anthems boom out in the arena. The big question is what has Canelo got left? In his prime, he'd have taken down Mbilli, no questions asked. But the champion is a fearsome volume puncher and Canelo's tendency to pot shot and pinch rounds in this stage of his career could leave him overwhelmed unless he makes a dent in Mbilli early. It's an intriguing clash. Jaime Munguia (c) vs. Nikita Zon for the WBA super middleweight title Jaime Munguia retains WBA super middleweight title via unanimous decision 5:29 p.m. ET - Munguia gets it by margins of 116-112 and 117-111 (twice) on the cards. A job well done in the end. That sixth round will live long in the memory 5:25 p.m. ET - They get to the final bell and Munguia has probably closed out the win. Zon saw his chance in the sixth, couldn't take it and emptied the tank. He definitely has other big nights ahead of him. As for Munguia, even if he retains his title, he should think about dropping back down to middleweight. He does not punch hard enough to trouble the best at this weight and is far too easy for 12 stone men to hit him clean. 5:10 p.m. ET - We're somehow through nine and into the championship rounds. I have Zon ahead, but it'll be close. When they trade, the Russian looks the boss, but he's taking chunks of some rounds off and that could cost him. Understandably, after that epic sixth, they both look exhausted. The pace easing suits Munguia's more technically skilled offense. Defensively, both of these men are an open book. 4:56 p.m. ET - CHAOS IN ROUND SIX! Munguia stalks in to close the show but Zon nails him with a huge catch-counter left uppercut and he's all over the place. He goes down. Weeks calls a push. I think that should have been a knockdown but Munguia is on the brink of being stopped. Then back he comes, snapping Zon's head back with a right. Somehow Munguia ends the round on top. Round of the year? What do each of them have left? 4:54 p.m. ET - Does Munguia have the power to really hurt opponents at 168 pounds? Well, he closes round five with a booming overhand right that socks Zon on the point of the chin. The challenger has to hold on and might have a storm to come through when the action resumes. 4:45 p.m. ET - Boy, do we have a fight here, Zon's corner are applying an ice back to the right-hand side of his face. That's evidence of the left hooks Munguia keeps nailing him with. But Zon is walking through the champion's power at this stage and he's definitely having an effect when he lands. He's doing so from some awkward angles and a peach of an uppercut forced Munguia to retreat to the ropes at the end of round three.

item.title: Patriots Make Two Roster Moves Ahead of Dolphins Game
item.description: Patriots Make Two Roster Moves Ahead of Dolphins Game originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New England Patriots made two roster moves ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Miami Dolphins, adding depth at running back and wide receiver with multiple offensive players unavailable. Patriots sign RB Lan Larison to 53-man roster from the practice squad; Elevate WR Ryan Miller from practice squad to active roster: https://t.co/jvMwFqka8F https://t.co/MLjcGysDft — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 31, 2026 New England signed running back Lan Larison to the 53-man roster and elevated wide receiver Ryan Miller from the practice squad. Both moves come after the Patriots ruled out wide receiver A.J. Brown and running back TreVeyon Henderson for the Week 8 contest. Patriots downgrade A.J. Brown, TreVeyon Henderson & Marcus Bryant to out for NE vs. MIA. https://t.co/SfBea3LiQ3 — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 31, 2026 Brown's absence is another setback for a Patriots receiving corps that has struggled to stay healthy. The veteran missed four games after suffering a high ankle sprain in his New England debut before returning to the lineup for the team's previous two contests. However, Brown experienced another issue during Wednesday's practice when a knee flare-up prevented him from finishing the session. He did not participate Thursday or Friday, and the Patriots downgraded him from questionable to out Saturday. Brown also did not travel with the team to Miami. The Patriots will now have to move forward without the wide receiver for another game, leaving his availability for the team's upcoming schedule worth monitoring. New England also will be without Romeo Doubs (shoulder) and Mack Hollins (calf), who remain on injured reserve . That leaves DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams as the only three healthy wide receivers on the 53-man roster. Miller's elevation gives quarterback Drake Maye another option in the passing game. The wide receiver has 17 career NFL receptions for 254 yards and four touchdowns, providing some experience as New England works through its injury issues at the position. Larison's addition addresses another need with Henderson unavailable. The running back previously appeared in New England's season opener and gives the Patriots another option behind their remaining healthy backs. Henderson has recorded 203 rushing yards and one touchdown on 52 carries this season. His absence leaves more work available for the Patriots' other running backs, while Larison could also contribute on special teams. New England will need contributions from several players to account for its offensive absences when it takes on Miami on Sunday. item.title: Hamilton takes first pole for Ferrari at Mexico City Grand Prix
item.description: Lewis Hamilton is one of two drivers who could prevent Kimi Antonelli winning the world championship in Mexico [Getty Images] Lewis Hamilton took his first pole position for Ferrari and his first for more than three years at the Mexico City Grand Prix. The seven-time champion beat Mercedes' George Russell by 0.009 seconds as the two drivers who can potentially stop Kimi Antonelli clinching the world title on Sunday locked out the front row. Antonelli qualified fifth behind Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Red Bull's Max Verstappen, but will start fourth because of a one-place penalty for the Dutchman. The only way Antonelli can be prevented from winning the title is if Russell wins and the Italian finishes lower than ninth, or Hamilton does and he is out of the points. Hamilton's pole is his first since the 2023 Hungarian Grand Prix, three years and three months ago. He and Russell both went out early for their first runs and had to watch as their rivals sought and failed to beat them. Leclerc went first, falling short of Hamilton by 0.119secs. Antonelli was never on target but Verstappen was fastest of all after two sectors and on course to take pole. But the Dutchman locked up into the hairpin in the stadium section and ruined his lap. More to follow. How to follow Mexico City Grand Prix on the BBC Listen to Back at Base on BBC Sounds

item.title: What happened to Josh Hoover? Indiana QB pulled from game at halftime vs. Minnesota
item.description: What happened to Josh Hoover? Indiana QB pulled from game at halftime vs. Minnesota originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The No. 4 Indiana Hoosiers are in a close one against Minnesota at home. In the second half, it appeared as though Hoosier head coach Curt Cignetti has decided to change quarterbacks. Starting quarterback Josh Hoover did not come out with his team after halftime, as his backup, Grant Wilson, got the nod under center. Hoover did take a big hit before halftime, but it's unclear if Cignetti has benched Hoover or if it was due to an injury. Here's what you need to know about Hoover's situation in Bloomington. MORE: Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti's best quotes What happened to Josh Hoover? When both teams came out of the tunnel in the second half, Hoover initially was not seen on the sideline but eventually joined the team. Hoover was not the first-team quarterback when the Hoosiers started on offense. He did take a big shot before halftime, but it's unclear if it is a benching or if Hoover is injured. MORE: Why NC State should ignore red flags and hire Philip Rivers Is Josh Hoover injured? In his post-halftime interview with Jenny Dell, Cignetti was unclear, saying "we'll see who trots out here the second half." He added that his team is making a lot of uncharacteristic mistakes: Curt Cignetti spoke with @JennyDell_ about his QB situation entering the 2nd half Grant Wilson has replaced Josh Hoover pic.twitter.com/N4wp7vQwjA — CBS Sports College Football 🏈 (@CBSSportsCFB) October 31, 2026 Hoover went 8-for-9 in the first half for 119 yards with a touchdown. He also threw an interception on a ball that was tipped. item.title: Match Awards from Bayern Munich’s costly 2-2 Der Klassiker draw
item.description: (Photo by Adam Pretty/Getty Images) | Getty Images With Germany boss Jürgen Klopp in attendance, the top teams in the Bundesliga battled it out to a 2-2 draw. Bayern Munich blew the lead twice as Dortmund’s home crowd rallied their team to play with higher energy and intensity for most of the match. Konrad Laimer and Dayot Upamecano were the unlikely scoring heroes for Bayern, while Serhou Guirassy and Fábio Silva saved Dortmund. Jersey Swap : Die Verletzungswelle By the halftime whistle, Ismael Saibari was helped off the pitch with a squashed ankle, Serge Gnabry limped off with a non-contact muscle injury, and Jonas Urbig’s face was bleeding Bayern red (literally!). To make matters wor se, Michael Olise asked to be substituted late in the second half. With key players like Luis Díaz, Jamal Musiala, and Manuel Neuer s till recovering from various injuries, Bayern cannot afford to lose any more players to the injury bug. Unsurprisingly, Ni ko Kovač’s tactics featured a brutish mindset on defense paired with a flopping approach on offense. Do rtmund’s lack of counterattacking speed forced the match to be played in smaller spaces, making it difficult for either team to maintain possession or establish any kind of rhythm. Subsequently, Gregor Kobel’s stat sheet was the primary benefactor of the match, but even he had to be bailed out by his own woodwork to stop Harry Kane, Michael Olise, and Lennart Karl. Der Kaiser: No one For most of the match, it was not a particularly poor performance from Bayern’s defense. But in the crucial moments , there were mental and physical breakdowns that ruined Bayern’s chance at claiming three points and sitting alone at the top of the table. K onrad Laimer and Dayot Upamecano were the best of the bunch, but their offensive contributions were more important . Kim Min-jae was erratic, Alphonso Davies started strong but was a non-factor on the back end, and Josi p Stanišić added another middling performance to his season. Fußballgott: Joshua Kimmich Playing in his first game since the unexpected passing of his father, team captain Joshua Kimmich delivered an emotional performance. After the Dortmund goal that drew the match level, Kimmich focused his team’s energy and sent the key pass to an unmarked Harry Kane, who calmly headed the ball back across the face of the goal to a surging Dayot Upamecano for the key moment. item.title: Zion Suzuki horror own goal haunts Aston Villa to hand Fulham equaliser
item.description: Fulham helped cement Jamie Carragher’s argument that Aston Villa will never be Manchester United. No, they know how to grind out a point on a bad day and can go to Barcelona on Tuesday with some confidence. Zion Suzuki’s own goal denied Unai Emery’s team a fifth win in six games after Nicolas Jackson’s eighth goal of the season had promised to lift a resurgent Villa back into the top third of the Premier League. item.title: 5 Best Nintendo Switch Games That Desperately Need Switch 2 Upgrades, Ranked
item.description: The Nintendo Switch 2 has been on one heck of run through launch. Though it has yet to see new installments of some heavy-hitter franchises, Nintendo’s latest console has built up an impressive library of games over its first year and a half. A chunk of that list includes excellent Nintendo Switch 2 Editions of the Switch’s best games. Super Mario Bros. Wonder , Kirby and the Forgotten Land , and more have gotten substantial updates that have helped make great Nintendo games even better. That trend is continuing too, as evidenced by the upcoming Pikmin 4 — Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy .

item.title: All that glitters is gold for Daphne Weller, girls' cross country state champion
item.description: TERRE HAUTE – Daphne Weller said she waited until the Stairway to Heaven to make her move. And when she did, it was glorious. The Fort Wayne Concordia Lutheran junior followed in the spikeprints of sister Mallory, running to a cross-country state championship Saturday. Moreover, Daphne set a 5,000-meter state meet record of 16 minutes, 52.2 seconds, the fastest ever by an Indiana high school girl on the iconic LaVern Gibson Championship course. The outcome followed an autumn of self-doubt, journaling and defeats. Daphne said she spent Friday night texting Mallory, a two-time national champion and now a freshman for North Carolina State’s reigning NCAA champions. “She definitely helped me through this,” Daphne said. Daphne twice lost races in September, including one in which she was beaten by three girls from the same school, Ann Arbor (Mich.) Pioneer. But she was fifth at state last fall and eighth as a freshman, so she knew the course and the stage. And she had witnessed her sister win this. “With this race, I just know I can, and I know I’m capable,” she said. “Your mind-set is so much stronger than anything else in running.” That “stairway” is what Concordia Lutheran coach Scott Steffen calls the distance from the 2- to 3-kilometer mark on this course. Daphne Weller stayed off the pace – “I didn’t want to burn myself out” – until she knew she could no longer wait. “Once I got around them,” she said, “I just took it to the finish.” Previous state meet record was 17:06.7 by Indian Creek’s Libby Dowty, who did so in winning the first of her two state titles in 2023. Dowty also held the best Indiana time of 16:55.7, set in last year’s Nike XC Town Twilight race. Terre Haute North sophomore Addyson Bautista was just off the state meet record, clocking 17:06.8 for second. Hamilton Southeastern junior Anya Zoeller was third in 17:08.0 after placing sixth last year for Pendleton Heights. “I stayed in the back of the pack and went at the end,” Zoeller said. Carmel’s Annabel Pollert was fourth in 17:21.8. Columbia City’s Kenya Leitch, who beat Daphne Weller by 21 seconds in a Sept. 16 meet, was fifth in 17:26.0. Zoe Gebhardt, also of HSE, was sixth in 17:33.3 and Heritage Christian freshman Aliyah Yorek seventh in 17:33.9. In team standings, Lake Central won its first state championship in this sport with 136 points, a record high score. (Previous high was 134 by Concordia Lutheran in 1983.) Homestead was second with 151 and two-time defending champion Carmel third with 176. Floyd Central was fourth with 207. Guerin Catholic also had 207 but was fifth on a tiebreaker – top No. 6 runner – for its first podium finish. Guerin’s top finisher was Lilly Higgins in 13 th . Coach Andy Cowan said the outcome was the culmination of a program built by former coach Tom Gallagher. “The group of girls we had this year was a really talented group, a really gritty group,” Cowan said. “And a resilient group, too. I just tried to get them to the line at the state meet h

In team standings, Lake Central won its first state championship in this sport with 136 points, a record high score. (Previous high was 134 by Concordia Lutheran in 1983.) Homestead was second with 151 and two-time defending champion Carmel third with 176. Floyd Central was fourth with 207. Guerin Catholic also had 207 but was fifth on a tiebreaker – top No. 6 runner – for its first podium finish. Guerin’s top finisher was Lilly Higgins in 13 th . Coach Andy Cowan said the outcome was the culmination of a program built by former coach Tom Gallagher. “The group of girls we had this year was a really talented group, a really gritty group,” Cowan said. “And a resilient group, too. I just tried to get them to the line at the state meet healthy, and knew we would be in the mix to potentially be in the top five. “They were ready for the moment.” So, as it turns out, was the latest Weller state champion. “Everybody has their own timeline,” she said. “Focus on myself and what I could work on instead of comparing myself to other people.” Contact David Woods at dwoods1411@gmail.com . item.title: Second-half blitz helps Saracens beat Newcastle
item.description: Saracens have not lost a Prem game at home to Newcastle since December 2007 [Shutterstock] The Prem Saracens (7) 39 Tries: George, Va'enuku, Knight, Tompkins, Caluori, Daly, Segun Cons: Farrell 2 Newcastle (17) 31 Tries: Kok, Graham, Hodge, Hearle Cons: Hodge 4 Pen: Hodge A dominant second-half display from Saracens saw them move back into the top-four as they overcame Newcastle Red Bulls with a bonus-point triumph at the Stone X Stadium. Tries from Werner Kok and Sam Graham had given the Red Bulls a 10-point cushion at half-time with Jamie George's try sandwiched in between as they went in search of successive wins. But a loss of discipline from the vistors in the second period changed the game as Graham and Alex Hearle were both yellow-carded. In the 17-minute spell in which Saracens had at least a one-man advantage, they scored 22 unanswered points with tries from Sione Va'enuku, Toby Knight, Nick Tompkins and Noah Caluori. Further scores from Elliot Daly and Rotimi Segun followed to make the game safe before two late efforts from Ollie Leatherbarrow and Hearle grabbed Newcastle a bonus point. But despite that, a fourth loss in five matches sends them into the November break bottom of the Prem. Saints come from behind to beat in-form Gloucester Cokanasiga scores twice as Bath overcome Sale Quins claim victory at Exeter in nine-try nailbiter Newcastle's Scotland prop Elliot Millar-Mills limped off inside the first five minutes, seven days away from New Zealand's visit to Murrayfield in the first of the Nations Championship matches next month. But the Red Bulls confidence from an opening win against Sale Sharks eight days ago was evident as they shrugged off that setback with Josh Hodge kicking an early penalty and minutes later Kok came off his wing and charged right through the middle of the defence for his second Prem try. Sarries, with 10 changes from the side that lost the London derby to Harlequins in disappointing fashion, took time to warm to the task but it was old hand George who got them on the board, getting it down at the back of a maul as the forwards drove over from a five-metre lineout. However, a sense of adventure allowed Newcastle to pull further clear with Hodge attacking the line and releasing Kok. The South African appeared to be tackled and falling into touch only for a sensational offload to Graham, who went over in the corner. But it was a different story after the break. Graham was sin-binned for killing a ruck not far from his own line and with him off the field, Va'enuku crossed. Then Hearle was punished for a deliberate knock-on and with two players extra, Knight went over and Tompkins and Caluori both crossed before Newcastle could get back to parity. By now, the momentum was completely with Saracens and Daly and Segun got their names on the scoresheet. However, the Red Bulls showed commendable spirit to find two tries in the last five minutes through new Scotland call-up Leatherbarrow and Hearle as the rebuilt side

Sarries, with 10 changes from the side that lost the London derby to Harlequins in disappointing fashion, took time to warm to the task but it was old hand George who got them on the board, getting it down at the back of a maul as the forwards drove over from a five-metre lineout. By now, the momentum was completely with Saracens and Daly and Segun got their names on the scoresheet. However, the Red Bulls showed commendable spirit to find two tries in the last five minutes through new Scotland call-up Leatherbarrow and Hearle as the rebuilt side maintained a record of picking up a point or better in all five of their Prem games so far. 'Opportunity to win slipped away from us' - reaction Saracens head coach Joe Shaw said: "It's probably best to forget about that first-half because it wasn't a pretty watch and was unexpected. "Red Bulls did what they had to do to stop us getting across their line but I can't remember seeing the team make so many handling errors. "We left so many chances out there on the field and it made things much harder for us than they should have been. "Fortunately, the guys improved a lot with their execution after the break and we created several fine tries." Newcastle Red Bulls head coach Dan McFarland told BBC Radio Newcastle: "Ultimately, it was very disappointing. In the first half we felt we did a lot of very good stuff, in particular around our defending. But we hadn't made the most of our opportunities. "But in the second half, two yellow cards against us - so we played nearly 20 minutes with 14 and even a chunk with 13 - and they scored four tries in that period. That's what changed the course of the game. "We're sat in the dressing room and we're disappointed because that was a game we had an opportunity get a grasp of and we let it slip away." Newcastle: Hodge; Wade, Hearle, Rigg, Kok; Connon, Benitez Cruz; Rakete-Stones, McGuigan, Millar Mills, Usher, Jordan, Hicks, Christie (c), Graham. Replacements: Adejimi, West, Moreno, Baker, Leatherbarrow, J Elliott, Henry, Harris. Sin-bin: Graham (45), Hearle (52) Referee: Ian Tempest

item.title: Freddie James, Legendary Texas High School Football Coach Portrayed in “Friday Night Lights”, Dies at 89
item.description: Freddie James Credit: PVAMU Office of Alumni Relations, University Advancement/Facebook NEED TO KNOW Freddie James, the legendary Texas high school football coach, died on Oct. 29 at age 89 He led Dallas’ Carter High School to 139 wins between 1982 and 1995, including the legendary 1988 championship that was later stripped James’ coaching legacy, which included sending eight players to the NFL, also inspired two films, including Friday Night Lights Freddie James, one of the most iconic coaches in the history of Texas high school football, has died. The legendary coach — who established a football dynasty at Dallas’ Carter High School in the ‘80s and ‘90s, earning nationwide attention and inspiring the film Friday Night Lights — died on Thursday, Oct. 29, according to his obituary . He was 89. James steered the Carter Cowboys as head football coach from 1982 to 1995, during which the team became a well-known powerhouse and raked in a total of 139 wins, according to USA Today and NBC 5 Dallas-Fort Worth . He also saw eight players reach the NFL, including New York Giants legend Jessie Armstead and Chet Brooks, who died earlier this year. James’ championship-winning 1988 team — which included Armstead — is widely regarded as the greatest high school football team in Texas history, though the victory was later marred by controversy when the title was stripped after a player was found to be ineligible. Freddie James in the image used in his obituary Credit: dignitymemorial The University Interscholastic League (UIL) formally stripped the title in 1991, per The Dallas Morning News — though James said he was not particularly bothered by the loss of the championship trophy. “It didn’t worry me. We proved on the field who was the best. I wasn’t worried about the trophy,” the late coaching icon said, according to the News . “That’s just a thing. In the mind of the people, Carter High School was the best team.” “We were the greatest that particular night,” added James, who was known for coaching with a lollipop in his mouth. It was the supporters of the Carter dynasty who mattered the most to James, not the title. Per the News , he said: “A lot of people in the Carter community told me, ‘It’s just a plaque. Coach, you hold your head up high. Don’t let this put you in the grave. There’s always tomorrow.’ ” James was inducted into the Texas Black Sports Hall of Fame class in 1996 as part of its inaugural class and later inducted into the Dallas Independent School District (ISD) Athletic Hall of Fame in 2018, according to the News . The legendary Carter coach’s legacy was honored with two films inspired by his coaching career and football dynasty: 2004’s Friday Night Lights , which spawned several seasons of an acclaimed TV series , and 2015’s Carter High . James was played by Julius Tennon and Charles S. Dutton in the films, respectively. Carter High School in Dallas, where Freddie James was a football coach in the ‘80s and ‘90s The day after James’ death, Carter High School football honored the late coaching icon on the field, under Friday night lights, according to NBC 5. At the game, the Dallas school’s current head coach, Spencer Gilbert, said that James “let me know that it’s not about the wins and losses; it’s about the legacy of people you impact along the way.” “Coach James was more than a football coach,” Gilbert said, according to NBC 5. “He was a mentor, he was father, a grandfather. Everything you asked a man to do.” Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE’s free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories. James graduated from Booker T. Washington High School with a scholarship to Prairie View A&M University in Prairie View, Texas, where he played on the school’s 1958 national championship team at both running back and defensive back, according to his obituary. He later got his start as a coach at Spigner High School in 1964 in Calvert, Texas. He married his college sweetheart, Eva June Jackson, who died in 2018, according to the News . He is survived by his son, Frenanda, and three grandchildren, as well as a great-granddaughter. Read the original article on People

item.title: Benvenuto Cellini wins Breeders' Cup Turf
item.description: Jockey Ryan Moore, seated aboard Benvenuto Cellini, celebrates after winning the Breeders' Cup Turf at Keeneland Horse Track (Tanner Pearson) Benvenuto Cellini won the $5 million Breeders' Cup Turf at Keeneland on Saturday, giving Irish trainer Aidan O'Brien a 24th Breeders' Cup victory. O'Brien came into this year's 14-race, $34 million Breeders' Cup festival in Lexington, Kentucky, tied with Bob Baffert for most wins by a trainer with 21. He bagged his third of the week after also saddling winners in the Juvenile Fillies Turf and Juvenile Turf on Friday. Baffert also nabbed a victory on Friday, in the Juvenile, but Ireland's O'Brien will depart Kentucky atop the Breeders' Cup trainers' table after an outstanding performance from jockey Ryan Moore aboard Benvenuto Cellini -- the Irish Derby winner who had finished a disappointing ninth in the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe earlier this month. Moore was threading through the field as they turned for home in the 1 1/2-mile race and was on the rail heading into the final furlong, springing to the outside and powering to the front to finish ahead of Map of Stars and stablemate Diamond Necklace. "Ryan gave him a brilliant ride," O'Brien said after bagging his eighth Turf win. "We've always felt he was a horse for this race. We felt he was very unlucky in the Arc, a lot more unlucky than anyone thought." O'Brien was also pleased with Diamond Necklace, Europe's leading three-year-old filly this year and a four-time group one winner. "Very difficult on a three-year-old filly after having the campaign she had, and (she) ran a stormer as well," he said. "So what can I say? Delighted and thankful to everybody." Ethical Diamond, who pulled off an upset victory in the same race last year at Del Mar, was never a factor in the repeat bid, breaking from the inside post but enduring a tough trip under jockey Dylan McMonagle. bb/js
