item.title: Viktor Arvidsson proving to be productive free-agent signing by Wings
item.description: DETROIT — There aren't too many lists or polls yet, signifying who has been the best free-agent signing this season by an NHL team. But if there were, Viktor Arvidsson would be near the top of the list. The Red Wings signed Arvidsson on July 1 to essentially replace Patrick Kane, who moved on to Chicago. So far, Arvidsson has been more than an adequate replacement. Arvidsson didn't get on the scoresheet in the 5-4 loss against St. Louis on Saturday, Oct. 31. But with 14 points (eight goals, six assists) in 14 games, Arvidsson has been a point per game player who has ably filled his role. Arvidsson felt the Wings were a good fit, having played for coach Todd McLellan when the pair were with the Los Angeles Kings. "Just Todd and that kind of thing," Arvidsson said of what appealed to him. "They needed some five-on-five scoring, and I saw myself providing that and some experience. I'm just trying to do my part and work hard and try to go to the net as much as I can." Arvidsson has always been an effective player around the net, but the Wings are seeing why each and every game. There's a ferocity, a will, and determination to the get to the tough areas and find any loose pucks that are lying aroud. "He's an energizer," McLellan said. "There's no neutral. You're either giving off energy and making others around you excited and energized, or you're sucking it out. There really is no neutral. "If you're on the positive side, the more guys we can have on the positive side, the better off we are. Arvy's indicator is almost always on the positive side because he does do those things. He's fearless, goes to the paint. He knows where he has to go to score goals. "If I'm one of the others on our team or any team and I haven't scored in a while, I probably pay attention to him." Sandin-Pellikka back in Grand Rapids It was bound to happen with the way defenseman Axel Sandin-Pellikka was being used — or rather, not being used. Sandin-Pellikka had only played in seven games, with one assist, and was averaging 12 minutes, 42 seconds of playing time. The development, and impressive play, of rookies Anton Johansson and William Wallinder pushed Sandin-Pellikka down the depth chart and the 2023 first-round draft pick needs to play. So, the Wings sent Sandin-Pellikka to Grand Rapids and recalled veteran Jacob Bernard-Docker . McLellan wanted Sandin-Pellikka to see more game action, but the Wings' current lineup wasn't going to allow it. "We're probably not dealing with it very well because he has been sitting and Axe needs to play now," McLellan said. "We also have to make decisions based on our lineup and we like what we're seeing from some players and how they're playing together. So unfortunately, when you don't go 11 (forwards and seven defensemen), there’s a D-man that sits out. When you go 12 (forwards) and six (defensemen), you have two (defensemen) sitting out. "It's been tough. He has to play." Ice chips Saturday's loss to the Blues was the first game the Wing

item.title: Undav unfazed by Bundesliga goal drought as Stuttgart claim important win over Leverkusen
item.description: Undav unfazed by Bundesliga goal drought as Stuttgart claim important win over Leverkusen VfB Stuttgart claimed three much-needed points in the Bundesliga with a 4-2 victory over Bayer Leverkusen on Saturday. Captain Deniz Undav provided a neat assist, but was unable to end his Bundesliga goal drought, having yet to score in the league this season. However, the striker insisted that his lack of goals was the least of his concerns. “It's completely irrelevant to me. First, we need to get out of this difficult period. Once things start going better again, the goals will come too,” Undav told Sky after the game. “I'm happy that we won – that's the most important thing. I'm proud of the team for the performance we put in. Given what we've been through recently, it wasn't easy,” the 30-year-old added. His goal drought is limited to the Bundesliga, as Undav has scored twice in all competitions this season. He last found the net in Wednesday's 1-0 DFB-Pokal win over SC Paderborn.

item.title: Here’s what Geno Auriemma thinks about Dream-Valkyries WNBA Finals Game 7
item.description: Robert Edwards-Imagn Images Here’s what Geno Auriemma thinks about Dream-Valkyries WNBA Finals Game 7 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . UConn women’s basketball coach Geno Auriemma is no stranger to high-stakes women’s basketball games, and he weighed in on the upcoming Game 7 of the WNBA Finals. Following a dominant victory by the Atlanta Dream on Thursday, the Valkyrie and the Dream are facing off in a winner-take-all Game 7 that is the first in WNBA history. Auriemma said the winner-take-all matchup should be memorable, particularly because it guarantees a first-time champion. “It’s gonna be pretty amazing, I think. Either way, whoever wins, it’s great when you have a first-time winner, right?” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Asked about Kiah Stokes being a frontrunner for Finals MVP, he said she’d put the title ahead of the individual award. “I think she would rather win tonight than be MVP. I’m sure she’d rather do both. She’ll be ready.” He then warned that points will be hard to come by, since both teams are strong defensively, and that the game could turn on an unexpected scorer. “It’s not gonna be easy. Both teams have such a hard time scoring because both defenses are so good. So I think whoever gets on a little bit of a roll offensively, somebody makes a bunch of shots, somebody steps out, then you go, ‘Where’d they come from?’” To illustrate the point, Auriemma recalled a game with Tiffany Hayes against Louisville, then a freshman on at UConn, had a breakout night. “I remember when Tiffany was on the team and she was a freshman and we played Louisville, and Walsh didn’t guard her, and she had 28. He said, ‘Well, we gotta pick somebody.’ And she came out of nowhere.” He also spoke about the key to game 7 that he believes no one will see coming. “So I’m sure in tonight’s game, they have the scouting report, they have the plan, they’ve got everything wired, but somebody’s gonna come out of nowhere and have everybody go, ‘That’s why we won.’ We just don’t know who that is. And if you don’t have that person, you’re probably gonna lose.” Related: Dream vs. Valkyries bold predictions for 2026 WNBA Finals Game 7 Related: Why Dream’s Angel Reese has ‘no doubt’ Atlanta will force a Game 7 vs. Valkyries

item.title: Brighton stun Man City, 10-man Man Utd beaten by Chelsea
item.description: Brighton beat Manchester City away for the first time in the club's history (Darren Staples) Brighton inflicted a second straight Premier League defeat on Manchester City with a 1-0 win to close within two points of the leaders on Saturday, while Manchester United slumped to another damaging defeat for Michael Carrick at Chelsea. Third-placed Brighton ended their wait for a first away win against City at the 18th attempt to bolster dreams of challenging for the title. The Seagulls have never won a major trophy but have already beaten champions Arsenal convincingly this season to show their title credentials. Fabian Hurzeler's men got revenge for defeat to City on penalties in the League Cup on Wednesday. Hurzeler felt aggrieved at that result after his side twice led at the Etihad. This time they held on after Yasin Ayari slotted them into an 11th-minute lead. Bart Verbruggen was inspired in the Brighton goal to see off a City onslaught after half-time. "We expected a game where we had to suffer. Coming to this place is very difficult, facing one of the best teams in the world," said Hurzeler. "I'm really proud of how my players stuck together. They had a little bit of luck but, in the end, deserved it." City won their opening seven league games as Enzo Maresca made a flawless start to the daunting task of succeeding Pep Guardiola. However, the 10-time English champions know their results on the field may count for little this season unless they can successfully overturn a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules. City have appealed, but if that ruling is upheld they are likely to face a severe points penalty and possible relegation from the English top-flight. "In this moment we are conceding silly goals that we can avoid," said Maresca. "I think we did enough to deserve something but we need to move on and try to win games." Defeat for City means Arsenal can go top of the table if they avoid losing at Liverpool on Sunday. - Man Utd self-implode - Manchester United's nine-game winless run is their longest without victory for 38 years after a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea. The Red Devils were left to regret not taking advantage of a series of first half chances to take the lead before they imploded in the second period to sit outside the relegation zone only on goal difference. Morgan Rogers was allowed to run straight through the heart of the United defence to open the scoring. Lisandro Martinez then did his under-pressure manager no favours with two quickfire yellow cards, the second of which also conceded a penalty. Cole Palmer converted from the spot to lift Chelsea into the top four. "The two halves of football couldn't probably be further apart," said Carrick, who added he expects to be in charge for Tuesday's Champions League tie against Roma. They had a little bit of luck but, in the end, deserved it." City won their opening seven league games as Enzo Maresca made a flawless start to the daunting task of succeeding Pep Guardiola. However, the 10-time English champions know their results on the field may count for little this season unless they can successfully overturn a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules. City have appealed, but if that ruling is upheld they are likely to face a severe points penalty and possible relegation from the English top-flight. "In this moment we are conceding silly goals that we can avoid," said Maresca. "I think we did enough to deserve something but we need to move on and try to win games." Defeat for City means Arsenal can go top of the table if they avoid losing at Liverpool on Sunday. - Man Utd self-implode - Manchester United's nine-game winless run is their longest without victory for 38 years after a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea. The Red Devils were left to regret not taking advantage of a series of first half chances to take the lead before they imploded in the second period to sit outside the relegation zone only on goal difference. Morgan Rogers was allowed to run straight through the heart of the United defence to open the scoring. Lisandro Martinez then did his under-pressure manager no favours with two quickfire yellow cards, the second of which also conceded a penalty. Cole Palmer converted from the spot to lift Chelsea into the top four. "The two halves of football couldn't probably be further apart," said Carrick, who added he expects to be in charge for Tuesday's Champions League tie against Roma. "We looked in a good place going into half-time and then found a way of unravelling it second half." Crystal Palace may beat United to a managerial change after Pierre Sage's side were easily beaten 2-0 at Tottenham to remain in the relegation zone. "It’s a disaster for every club in the Premier League," said Sage on the prospect of relegation. "I’m not comfortable with the position but it’s a consequence of what we have done on the pitch." Jean-Philippe Mateta's early red card for a lunge on Micky van de Ven left the Eagles a mountain to climb. In keeping with Sage's time in charge, it was Palace's inability to deal with set-pieces that saw Spurs claim a third consecutive win. Archie Gray headed in unmarked from a corner before Jan Paul van Hecke bundled in the second after his initial attempt was brilliantly saved by Dean Henderson. After a difficult start, a resurgent Tottenham are up to eighth. Aston Villa's surge up the table stalled in a 1-1 draw against Fulham due to an own goal from goalkeeper Zion Suzuki. The in-form Nicolas Jackson put Unai Emery's men in front before Suzuki, who had made a string of excellent saves, fumbled Alex Iwobi's corner over the goalline. Oliver Glasner vowed to make sweeping changes after a 2-0 defeat at Brentford saw Nottingham Forest slip to 19th. Bournemouth were also 2-0 winners over Leeds, while Sunderland remain rooted to the foot of the table after a 3-1 loss at Coventry. Hull and Ipswich played out a 2-2 draw. kca/lp

item.title: Ortom hits back at ex-envoy Tarzoor, highlights governance achievements
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi Former Benue State Governor, Chief Samuel Ortom, has challenged Ambassador Terhemen Tarzoor to account for his record in public office, accusing him of sustained attacks on his person over the defeat he suffered during the 2015 governorship election in the state. Recall that the former Nigerian envoy to Namibia had, during a recent media outing criticised the former governor over what he described as uncomplimentary remarks about Governor Hyacinth Alia and his administration. Ortom described Tarzoor’s criticism as “a manifestation of the bitterness he has harboured since his defeat in the 2015 governorship election,” alleging that the former governorship candidate had consistently used media engagements to attack him more than a decade after the election. He said Tarzoor’s latest comments, ostensibly in defence of Governor Hyacinth Alia, were an attempt to remain politically relevant. He added that the ambassador had misrepresented his remarks by claiming that he described the actions of the people of Benue as “shenanigans.” “Chief Ortom could never have used such a term to disparage the people of Benue State. If anything, his reference was to the antics of individuals like Tarzoor, whose utterances and conduct appear calculated to sow discord, deepen divisions and breed acrimony in the polity,” he said. Ina statement.by his media Aide, Paul Zege, the former governor questioned Tarzoor’s record as Speaker of the Benue State House of Assembly, asking him to identify the developmental projects he attracted to his constituency and the achievements he could point to as evidence of his contributions to the people. item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Okogba
item.content:encoded: By Peter Duru, Makurdi Former Benue State Governor, Chief Samuel Ortom, has challenged Ambassador Terhemen Tarzoor to account for his record in public office, accusing him of sustained attacks on his person over the defeat he suffered during the 2015 governorship election in the state. Recall that the former Nigerian envoy to Namibia had, during a recent media outing criticised the former governor over what he described as uncomplimentary remarks about Governor Hyacinth Alia and his administration. Ortom described Tarzoor’s criticism as “a manifestation of the bitterness he has harboured since his defeat in the 2015 governorship election,” alleging that the former governorship candidate had consistently used media engagements to attack him more than a decade after the election. He said Tarzoor’s latest comments, ostensibly in defence of Governor Hyacinth Alia, were an attempt to remain politically relevant. He added that the ambassador had misrepresented his remarks by claiming that he described the actions of the people of Benue as “shenanigans.” “Chief Ortom could never have used such a term to disparage the people of Benue State. If anything, his reference was to the antics of individuals like Tarzoor, whose utterances and conduct appear calculated to sow discord, deepen divisions and breed acrimony in the polity,” he said. Ina statement.by his media Aide, Paul Zege, the former governor questioned Tarzoor’s record as Speaker of the Benue State House of Assembly, asking him to identify the developmental projects he attracted to his constituency and the achievements he could point to as evidence of his contributions to the people. He also raised questions about the controversial creation of a Fulani ward in Makurdi Local Government Area, LGA, which he said was subsequently reversed after the exercise was reportedly found to be fraudulent. Ortom further questioned Tarzoor’s record as Nigeria’s ambassador to Namibia, alleging that his tenure failed to establish a notable diplomatic legacy, urging the former Speaker to focus on issues affecting the state rather than engage in what he described as persistent attacks on him. Defending his administration’s record, Ortom said security was one of the defining issues of his tenure, particularly his opposition to open grazing and the repeated attacks on farming communities. He said his administration “enacted the Open Grazing Prohibition and Ranches Establishment Law of 2017, established the Benue State Livestock Guards, supported the Community Volunteer Guards and provided logistics to security agencies. “He could have chosen the politically convenient path. He could have remained silent, avoided confrontation with powerful interests and maintained cordial relations with the Federal Government of the day. Instead, he chose to stand with his people and defend their lands when he believed the survival of his people was at stake,” he said. On education, Ortom listed the execution of more than 1,000 primary school projects in collaboration with the Universal Basic Education Commission, the provision of desks and other learning materials, the renovation of secondary schools and the upgrading of some tertiary institutions. He said his administration also ‘introduced a first-line funding arrangement for Benue State University, BSU, to improve its financial stability and supported the accreditation of its College of Health Sciences, enabling medical students to graduate.” On healthcare, Ortom said his administration supported the revival and accreditation of the Schools of Nursing and Midwifery in Makurdi and the School of Health Technology, Agasha. Other interventions, according to him, included the establishment of the Benue State Health Insurance Scheme and the Primary Health Care Board, the provision of 42 health centres, ambulances and medical equipment, as well as investments in facilities at the Benue State University Teaching Hospital. Ortom also disputed allegations that he failed to execute infrastructure projects during his eight years in office, listing roads constructed or rehabilitated in Makurdi, Gboko, Otukpo and other parts of the state. Among the projects he cited were the 47-kilometre Zaki-Biam-Gbeji-Afia Road, the Agatu-Oshigbudu-Obagaji Road, the 30-kilometre Gbajimba-Iordye-Akaahena feeder road, as well as several urban roads and rural bridges. On agriculture and rural development, he said his administration provided fertiliser to farmers at a 50 per cent subsidy for eight cropping seasons, acquired 50 tractors for distribution at a 60 per cent subsidy and collaborated with the International Fund for Agricultural Development on farmer training and the provision of improved seedlings. He also cited the revival of the fertiliser blending plant, the construction of agro-processing factories in six LGAs and the introduction of a Friday work-free farming initiative during critical agricultural seasons. The former governor further listed the provision of more than 1,000 motorised and hand-pump water schemes, the completion of over 60 electricity projects, the rehabilitation of public facilities and the construction of palaces for the Tor Tiv in Gboko and the Och’Idoma in Otukpo. He said his administration also established the Benue Geographic Information Service, strengthened public procurement and debt management institutions, domesticated the Treasury Single Account and introduced reforms aimed at improving government revenue administration. Ortom acknowledged that his administration had shortcomings but argued that these should not be used to dismiss its entire record. He said his administration faced difficult economic conditions,”including two recessions and the COVID-19 pandemic, while grappling with insecurity and the displacement of farming communities.” According to him, salaries were paid for 91 of the administration’s 96 months despite the fiscal challenges. “Ortom was not a perfect governor. He has never claimed to be perfect. No honest assessment of his administration should pretend otherwise,” he said, adding that there was a difference between arguing that the former governor could have achieved more and claiming that he did nothing for eight years. He also cited his longstanding provision of free treatment for snakebite victims, which he said dated back to 2000 and continued throughout his years in public service. On the controversy surrounding the entitlements of former governors, Ortom said the matter should be determined by the applicable law rather than Tarzoor’s personal recollection of the legal framework during his tenure as Speaker. He challenged Tarzoor to identify the specific claims he considered false and provide verifiable evidence to contradict them, while urging the Alia administration to subject its own performance to public scrutiny. “Public accountability does not expire at the end of an administration, and criticism of a sitting governor is not proof of bitterness,” he said, urging Tarzoor to move beyond the 2015 governorship election and focus on issues affecting the development of Benue State. Ortom maintained that his record should be assessed on the basis of policies, projects, institutional reforms and the circumstances under which his administration operated, rather than political accusations. The post Ortom hits back at ex-envoy Tarzoor, highlights governance achievements appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Don’t be deceived, vote for Tinubu, South-East govs tell Igbos
item.description: Governors of Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu and Imo States have urged the people not to be deceived by political distractions but to vote massively for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election. The governors made the call on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) Women Mega Rally and Empowerment Programme for the South-East, held at Okpara Square, Enugu. The governors are Prof. Charles Soludo of Anambra, Francis Nwifuru of Ebonyi, Dr Peter Mbah of Enugu and Sen. Hope Uzodimma of Imo. Speaking, Mbah urged the people of the South-East to support Tinubu’s re-election bid to enable him to consolidate the gains of his administration’s economic reforms. He attributed ongoing development projects, including the construction of primary healthcare centres, to the Federal Government’s economic reforms. The governor urged women to support Tinubu and APC candidates in the Jan. 16, 2027, and subsequent elections. “A good sailor does not abandon his ship mid-sea because of challenges. We must finish the journey we all started together,” he said. Mbah described South Easterners as strategic people who had established businesses and relationships beyond the zone, urging them to participate actively in the political process. Speaking on the empowerment programme targeting 5,000 women across the South-East, Mbah said the initiative followed the empowerment of more than 2,000 women in Enugu within 48 hours. He said the beneficiaries received cash support, assistance with hospital bills and tools to enable them to generate income. According to him, the programme is designed to make women wealth creators rather than perpetual beneficiaries of financial assistance. “When you empower a woman, you strengthen the family. When you empower a woman, you build a strong community,” he said. He urged the beneficiaries to make effective use of the empowerment tools and extend the benefits to their families and communities. Also speaking, Uzodimma described the rally as historic and commended the First Lady, Sen. Oluremi Tinubu, for empowering women across the South-East. He reiterated the commitment of the region to supporting Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. He explained that Igbos had experienced marginalisation for over 60 years but were beginning to witness a new era of political inclusion and development under Tinubu. He commended the president for expanding the scope of infrastructural and economic development in the South-East. “We are now seeing good roads, electricity, and health reforms as well as educational reforms in the country. A winning team must not be changed,” he said. The governor urged the electorate to sustain the current development trajectory, saying the federal government’s economic reforms had increased resources available to states for development. “We have more money to build Okigwe to Owerri, Umuahia to Owerri, Orlu to Owerri and Owerri to Port Harcourt roads,” he said. The governors made the call on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) Women Mega Rally and Empowerment Programme for the South-East, held at Okpara Square, Enugu. The governors are Prof. Charles Soludo of Anambra, Francis Nwifuru of Ebonyi, Dr Peter Mbah of Enugu and Sen. Hope Uzodimma of Imo. Speaking, Mbah urged the people of the South-East to support Tinubu’s re-election bid to enable him to consolidate the gains of his administration’s economic reforms. He attributed ongoing development projects, including the construction of primary healthcare centres, to the Federal Government’s economic reforms. The governor urged women to support Tinubu and APC candidates in the Jan. 16, 2027, and subsequent elections. “A good sailor does not abandon his ship mid-sea because of challenges. We must finish the journey we all started together,” he said. Mbah described South Easterners as strategic people who had established businesses and relationships beyond the zone, urging them to participate actively in the political process. Speaking on the empowerment programme targeting 5,000 women across the South-East, Mbah said the initiative followed the empowerment of more than 2,000 women in Enugu within 48 hours. He said the beneficiaries received cash support, assistance with hospital bills and tools to enable them to generate income. According to him, the programme is designed to make women wealth creators rather than perpetual beneficiaries of financial assistance. “When you empower a woman, you strengthen the family. When you empower a woman, you build a strong community,” he said. He urged the beneficiaries to make effective use of the empowerment tools and extend the benefits to their families and communities. Also speaking, Uzodimma described the rally as historic and commended the First Lady, Sen. Oluremi Tinubu, for empowering women across the South-East. He reiterated the commitment of the region to supporting Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. He explained that Igbos had experienced marginalisation for over 60 years but were beginning to witness a new era of political inclusion and development under Tinubu. He commended the president for expanding the scope of infrastructural and economic development in the South-East. “We are now seeing good roads, electricity, and health reforms as well as educational reforms in the country. A winning team must not be changed,” he said. The governor urged the electorate to sustain the current development trajectory, saying the federal government’s economic reforms had increased resources available to states for development. “We have more money to build Okigwe to Owerri, Umuahia to Owerri, Orlu to Owerri and Owerri to Port Harcourt roads,” he said. Uzodimma added that the improved financial position of the state had enabled his administration to pay salaries and pensions consistently, including 13th-month salaries for workers. In his remarks, Nwifuru commended the skills acquisition and empowerment initiatives of the APC-led administration, urging South-East women to vote massively for the party. He described the APC as the only political party with a clear and identifiable manifesto capable of sustaining the country’s development. The governor dismissed suggestions of his involvement in any political coalition, stressing that his loyalty remained with the APC. He urged supporters to vote for APC candidates at all levels in the January 2027 elections and subsequent polls. Similarly, Soludo, represented by his Deputy, Dr Gilbert Ibezim, said the South-East had a responsibility to support Tinubu’s re-election in appreciation of his administration’s achievements. He said the region stood to benefit more from continued collaboration with the federal government. Also speaking, the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Mr Benjamin Kalu, urged Igbos to embrace political inclusion by supporting Tinubu’s re-election. Kalu said the Igbo had not produced a president of Nigeria in the past 60 years, stressing the need for the region to strengthen its political alliances. He recalled that Tinubu, while serving as governor of Lagos State, maintained cordial relationships with Igbos and included them in his cabinet. He commended the Tinubu administration for establishing the South East Development Commission (SEDC). He described it as a major step towards addressing the region’s developmental challenges. ( NAN ) The post 2027: Don’t be deceived, vote for Tinubu, South-East govs tell Igbos appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Barca hammer Alaves to retain Liga top spot
item.description: Giuliano Simeone was on target for Atletico Madrid as they beat Levante to move provisionally top of La Liga on Saturday (JOSE JORDAN) Raphinha and Lamine Yamal struck twice each as Barcelona thrashed Alaves 6-1 on Saturday to reclaim their La Liga lead and get back on track after two damaging defeats. Earlier Atletico Madrid, second, earned a solid 2-0 win at Levante, but Barca moved back two points clear of the Rojiblancos by routing the Basque visitors at Camp Nou. Still stinging after a Champions League defeat by Paris Saint-Germain and then last weekend's La Liga home Clasico loss against rivals Real Madrid, Hansi Flick's side found their groove once more. Raphinha netted twice in the first half, either side of a Fermin Lopez strike, and Yamal found the net just before the interval. Teenage winger Yamal netted again midway through the second half and substitute Anthony Gordon chipped home Barca's sixth, before Mariano Diaz pulled one back for Alaves. There was a minute's silence at the start of each of the day's matches in memory of the 69 victims of the train crash in the province of Toledo that rocked Spain this week. Flick lined up with Dutch midfielder Frenkie de Jong playing at centre-back and youngster Brian Farinas making his first start at right-back, amid a spate of defensive injuries. It did not hamper the champions. Barcelona moved ahead in the eighth minute, with La Liga's top scorer Raphinha continuing his red-hot form. Midfield maestro Pedri played in Lopez, who pulled the ball across for the Brazil international to bundle home. Alaves came close through Abde Rebbach before Lopez doubled Barcelona's lead in the 23rd minute. Yamal slipped the midfielder in and, from a tight angle, Lopez smashed the ball across goal and fortuitously in at the far post, seemingly intending to cross it. Karim Adeyemi and Yamal both missed glorious chances from close range to expand on Barca's lead, with Raphinha showing the duo how to do it as he bagged his 15th league goal. Lopez sent the forward through on goal and Raphinha produced a lethal finish across Antonio Sivera. Perhaps frustrated by his miss, Yamal smashed home the fourth with an instinctive low strike from the edge of the box in first half stoppage time. Adeyemi blazed another presentable chance over the crossbar early in the second half after Lopez unselfishly set him up. Yamal got Barca's fifth with a neat dink over the goalkeeper after substitute Gabriel Jesus played him through on goal. Gordon produced a similar finish for Barca's sixth and the only tarnish on their evening was former Real Madrid striker Diaz netting late on. - Seven in a row - Earlier in Valencia Diego Simeone's Atletico had temporarily climbed a point clear of the Catalan giants with goals from Alejandro Grimaldo and Giuliano Simeone against Levante. Teenage winger Yamal netted again midway through the second half and substitute Anthony Gordon chipped home Barca's sixth, before Mariano Diaz pulled one back for Alaves. There was a minute's silence at the start of each of the day's matches in memory of the 69 victims of the train crash in the province of Toledo that rocked Spain this week. Flick lined up with Dutch midfielder Frenkie de Jong playing at centre-back and youngster Brian Farinas making his first start at right-back, amid a spate of defensive injuries. It did not hamper the champions. Barcelona moved ahead in the eighth minute, with La Liga's top scorer Raphinha continuing his red-hot form. Midfield maestro Pedri played in Lopez, who pulled the ball across for the Brazil international to bundle home. Alaves came close through Abde Rebbach before Lopez doubled Barcelona's lead in the 23rd minute. Yamal slipped the midfielder in and, from a tight angle, Lopez smashed the ball across goal and fortuitously in at the far post, seemingly intending to cross it. Karim Adeyemi and Yamal both missed glorious chances from close range to expand on Barca's lead, with Raphinha showing the duo how to do it as he bagged his 15th league goal. Lopez sent the forward through on goal and Raphinha produced a lethal finish across Antonio Sivera. Perhaps frustrated by his miss, Yamal smashed home the fourth with an instinctive low strike from the edge of the box in first half stoppage time. Adeyemi blazed another presentable chance over the crossbar early in the second half after Lopez unselfishly set him up. Yamal got Barca's fifth with a neat dink over the goalkeeper after substitute Gabriel Jesus played him through on goal. Gordon produced a similar finish for Barca's sixth and the only tarnish on their evening was former Real Madrid striker Diaz netting late on. - Seven in a row - Earlier in Valencia Diego Simeone's Atletico had temporarily climbed a point clear of the Catalan giants with goals from Alejandro Grimaldo and Giuliano Simeone against Levante. Atletico recorded a seventh consecutive league win to continue their strong form and put pressure on the reigning champions. "I'm very happy with the team's work," Atletico coach Simeone told Movistar. "We're very far from the end of the season... we'll keep going game by game." Alex Baena, the visitors' main creative outlet, set up both goals as Simeone recorded his 344th La Liga win at the helm of Atletico, matching the club's record set by Luis Aragones. "I don't feel it much as mine, but it belongs to my players, everyone who has been with me for so many years," said Simeone, who started coaching Atletico in 2011. Atletico host Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Tuesday before welcoming Barca to the Metropolitano stadium next weekend in La Liga. On Sunday, Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid, third, visit Racing Santander among other fixtures. rbs/nf/dmc

item.title: Fort Collins boys surge to 3rd place at Colorado state cross-country
item.description: Another strong Fort Collins-area high cross-country season wrapped with an elite finish at the Colorado state meet. Fort Collins High School's Will Johns led a Lambkins surge, racing to third place in Class 5A boys as an individual and spurring the team to an impressive bronze finish Oct. 31 at Colorado Springs' Norris Penrose Event Center. Johns surged in the race's final portion, running the final 1.05 miles in a hair over 5 minutes. He crossed the finish line in 15:12.44, moving up from 12th to fifth to third throughout the race. The junior was just one second behind the runner-up and sixteen back of 5A boys champion Abdinasir Hassan from Northfield. Johns capped a phenomenal season as one of the state's top runners. He finished top-five in every Colorado event this season and won the Front Range League championship. Sean Giles was the next-best finisher from Fort Collins, taking 12th in 15:55.68. Fort Collins won a close race for third in the team standings, finishing with 156 points. That was just one ahead of Heritage (157) and two clear of Mountain Vista (158). Niwot was well clear, winning the 5A title with a mere 60 points. It was a fantastic showing for the Lambkins against an elite field that got even better with state power Niwot moving up to Class 5A. Here are the other Fort Collins scorers for the third-place squad: Owen Kirkpatrick (37th, 16:32.80) Oliver Singleton, (55th, 16:48.00) Tobin Rapley, (59th, 16:52.70) Fort Collins also had the top local team finish in the 5A girls race, finishing eighth with 270 points. These Lambkins girls placed in the top 50 runners: Brooke Johns (30th, 19:14.52) Emma Jones (37th, 19:24.68) Olive Giuliani (40th, 19:33.61) The Fossil Ridge girls finished 10th as a team in Class 5A with a pair of top-50 placers: Avery Breitigam (13th, 18:46.05) Maya DiGiallonardo (47th, 19:43.65) Rocky Mountain freshman Jordyn Grossnickle took 20th among 5A girls in 19:01.19. Rigby Ruffer led the Lobos in the 5A boys race, taking 30th in 16:22.40. Heritage Christian girls grab 3rd in Class 2A The Eagles finished third in a tight 2A girls team race, scoring 80 points to finish just five points back of champion Thomas Maclaren School (75) and two off runner-up Ridgway (78). Kate Lukens led the way with a second straight podium finish at state, placing ninth in 20:08.46. Heritage Christian's depth shone through, with all five Eagles scorers finishing inside the 2A girls top 50: Emma Lukens (30th, 21:17.11) Hailey Lukens (40th, 21:42.28) Maebelle Cheney (45th, 21:52.54) Elyse Robinson (50th, 22:07.03) HCA also earned a podium spot in the 2A boys race, with Lucas Delorme crossing in eighth in 16:50.25. Timnath leads local 4A finishers It wasn't a third straight title, but the Cubs had the only podium finisher among local runners. item.title: Julian Nagelsmann has already received Juventus’ call, INEOS need to act soon
item.description: Julian Nagelsmann has already received Juventus’ call, INEOS need to act soon Despite their disastrous run of form, Manchester United decided to stick with Michael Carrick following extensive crisis talks. There were murmurs that football director Jason Wilcox had approached Eddie Howe , but those reports proved premature as the former United midfielder remained at the helm . That decision has not worked out well, as the Red Devils lost 2-0 to Chelsea on Saturday. The first half was a more cohesive performance , but Lisandro Martinez single-handedly lost United the game . While Carrick November international break begins . Nagelsmann is a wanted man Recruitment chief Christopher Vivell has been advocating for Julian Nagelsmann, but the former Germany coach is a wanted man. RB Leipzig and Fenerbahce have been linked with the ex-Bayern Munich boss, and Juventus have now joined the race. According to journalist Rudy Galetti , “Juventus have just contacted Julian Nagelsmann, adding the German coach to their preferred alternatives should they decide to replace Spalletti. “The former Germany boss is weighing several options for his future and appreciated the Bianconeri’s approach.” Why INEOS are delaying the final call As things stand, Julian Nagelsmann seems to be slipping away from United’s grasp. But not everyone in the hierarchy would be too concerned about the loss. Many want the club to show some ambition and try to bring in project managers such as Cesc Fabregas or Unai Emery . Both are unlikely to make the jump mid-season, so a decision might have to wait for now. With Howe’s compensation claims set to reduce further and the current head coach ‘s break clause also due to activate, the penny-pinching co-owners have a choice to make. online polls

item.title: Prayers Pour In as Arizona Wide Receiver Carted Off the Field After Nasty Hit Against Texas Tech
item.description: Copyright: xx ZUMA-20221015_zaf_c04_276.jpg SeanxBrownx csmphototwo980630 ©IMAGO/Newscom World The Big 12 showdown between the Texas Tech Red Raiders and Arizona Wildcats was arguably one of Week 9’s most consequential games, but the action took a worrying turn in the third quarter. Arizona lost 34-26 to Texas Tech on Saturday, and in the third quarter, wide receiver R.J. Mosley suffered what looked like a knee injury. It happened on third-and-18, when Mosley caught a pass from quarterback Noah Fifita and was brought down by Texas Tech defensive back Amier Boyd after an eight-yard gain. Wildcats fans quickly sent prayers his way. The moment he landed, Mosley reached for his knee, and Fifita and a number of Arizona players rushed to respond. The broadcast footage shared by ESPN College Football X handle showed a horrific injury, with his knee seemingly dislocated or potentially broken. ESPN’s broadcast skipped the replay because the production truck decided the footage was too graphic to air. Wildcats players immediately gathered around their injured teammate as medical personnel stabilized his leg. Mosley was loaded onto a cart and taken off the field as the crowd watched in silence before applauding. He was seen smiling as he left. A devastating moment has shaken college football. Stay informed on Arizona's injury updates and game impact with EssentiallySports' latest coverage. The severity of the injury was enough to leave even seasoned insiders deeply concerned about the freshman wide receiver’s well-being. One insider couldn’t hide his concern, writing, “Oh man. Bad-looking leg injury for talented freshman wideout R.J. Mosley. You know it’s not good when they won’t show a replay.” Once it was clear how serious the injury looked, Arizona fans turned to social media to support the freshman receiver, posting prayers and messages of encouragement. A fan shared the video and wrote a heartfelt message, “Praying for RJ Mosley.” Another joined and sent prayers, writing, “Prayers to R.J. Mosley what a brutal-looking injury.” Fifita dropped to a knee and prayed as medical staff rushed to Mosley. The crowd watched in silence before erupting into applause as Mosley was carted off the field. The sight of teammates and players surrounding Mosley following the injury was heartbreaking, but for some fans, the scene itself raised serious concerns about the gravity of the situation. One fan pointed to the worrying image, writing, “Guys huddling up around him before the cart tells you enough. that’s never the scene you want to see” Others put their concerns aside to send their support and prayers to the injured wide receiver. One fan shared an emotional message, “SENDING PRAYERS AND HUGS TO U OF A RJ MOSLEY. 🌹” Taylor McGregor, ESPN’s sideline reporter, relayed early in the fourth quarter that Mosley was undergoing lower-body X-rays as medical staff worked to size up the injury. He was subsequently taken to a local hospital for further examination and treatment

item.title: 49ers’ Dre Greenlaw slapped with hefty fine for punching Falcons’ Drake London
item.description: 49ers star linebacker Dre Greenlaw has had a costly start to the season. NFL insider Tom Pelissero broke news on Saturday that Greenlaw has been fined $12,537 for unnecessary roughness against Falcons star wide receiver Drake London . Dre Greenlaw of the San Francisco 49ers stands on the sideline during a game against the Arizona Cardinals in Santa Clara, California, Sunday, Sept. 27, 2026. Getty Images Greenlaw tried to punch the ball out of London’s hands during the 49ers’ 29-20 loss to the Falcons last Sunday. Greenlaw’s punch missed its target, as he connected with London’s helmet instead. San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw loading up to punch the ball out of Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London’s hands. (X/@TomPelissero). No penalty was called on Greenlaw during the play, but video replays of the incident showed why Greenlaw ultimately got in trouble. London left the game to be evaluated for a concussion after the punch but was ultimately cleared and able to return. Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London (5) walks off the field after a game against the San Francisco 49ers in Atlanta, Georgia, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There is no reason to believe there was any malice behind Greenlaw’s punch, as it just didn’t connect where it was meant to. Greenlaw was fined $11,941 by the NFL for taunting the Broncos’ bench (specifically his former head coach, Sean Payton) earlier in the season. The star linebacker will surely hope to stop giving the league reasons to fine him once San Francisco returns from its bye week.

item.title: Barcelona star bags his first-ever assist for the club vs Alavés
item.description: Barcelona star bags his first-ever assist for the club vs Alavés A member of the midfield ranks at La Liga giants Barcelona on Saturday hit a long-awaited personal benchmark in the club’s colours. This came upon Rodri breaking his duck in the assists column in Blaugrana colours. Barcelona were of course back in action a short time ago, welcoming Deportivo Alavés to Catalunya’s capital for a league clash. Hansi Flick’s troops headed into proceedings desperate for a bounce-back result, following back-to-back defeats across all competitions. And when all was said and done, this is precisely what they managed, courtesy of a 6-1 romp. The aforementioned Rodri featured from the off in the fixture, from his berth at the base of midfield. And as alluded to above, during the 2nd-half, the 30-year-old hit a personal milestone for his new club. After laying on Anthony Gordon’s late 6th, Rodri registered his first-ever assist in the famed red and blue of Barcelona. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Suzuki's costly mistake as Villa draw with Fulham
item.description: Premier League Aston Villa 1 - 1 Fulham FT Aston Villa are unbeaten in their past five Premier League matches [Getty Images] Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki dropped the ball into his own net as Fulham had a helping hand in recovering to earn a Premier League draw at Villa Park. Striker Nicolas Jackson had earlier continued his fine scoring form for the hosts, but his first-half goal was not enough for victory because of Suzuki's costly error. The Japan international could not hold on to Alex Iwobi's inswinging corner midway through the second half and fumbled the ball narrowly over the line for an own goal. Villa were in good shape when Jackson got his sixth goal in all competitions in October - more than any other top-flight player. He raced on to Johan Manzambi's pass, evaded weak challenges from David Affengruber and Timothy Castagne, and slotted past Bernd Leno. That goal came in the 39th minute, and Villa should have gone ahead 23 minutes earlier when they were awarded a penalty. Leon Goretzka's header was handled by Sander Berge, with referee Sam Barrott originally missing the offence, only for video assistant referee Matthew Donohue to advise him to watch it n a pitchside monitor. Barrott changed his decision, but Villa captain John McGinn could not capitalise as his penalty bounced away off the crossbar. When it was goalless, Fulham nearly went ahead when Suzuki made a superb one-handed save to keep out Oscar Bobb's effort. Suzuki also denied Gonzalo Garcia in the second half, but he badly blundered for the equaliser and it ultimately proved costly for the hosts. Villa have now won three, drawn three and lost three of their nine league matches and are ninth in the table, three points and six places above Fulham in 15th. More to follow. That goal came in the 39th minute, and Villa should have gone ahead 23 minutes earlier when they were awarded a penalty. Leon Goretzka's header was handled by Sander Berge, with referee Sam Barrott originally missing the offence, only for video assistant referee Matthew Donohue to advise him to watch it n a pitchside monitor. Barrott changed his decision, but Villa captain John McGinn could not capitalise as his penalty bounced away off the crossbar. When it was goalless, Fulham nearly went ahead when Suzuki made a superb one-handed save to keep out Oscar Bobb's effort. Suzuki also denied Gonzalo Garcia in the second half, but he badly blundered for the equaliser and it ultimately proved costly for the hosts. Villa have now won three, drawn three and lost three of their nine league matches and are ninth in the table, three points and six places above Fulham in 15th. More to follow. item.description: Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) is live TONIGHT (Sat., Oct. 31, 2026) with UFC Halloween (a.k.a. UFC Vegas 123 ) , streaming live online via Paramount+ . The event goes down inside the familiar META APEX in Las Vegas, Nevada. Our main event on this Halloween event is Renato Moicano vs. Tom Nolan ( see betting odds here ). UFC Halloween Preview It feels a little odd to see a UFC fight night land on Halloween. It would be nice if UFC did something to dress up for the occasion, but knowing them it will probably be business as usual. Renato Moicano vs. Tom Nolan draw the short straw of being unable to go trick or treating with their kids this night ( are you? ). They are meeting in the main event, despite Moicano saying he was desperate to escape the APEX. UFC Halloween’s co-main event is DC’s boy Jacobe Smith taking on the veteran Randy Brown ( on super short notice ). Smith has decimated all who have stood in his way so far. If he runs through Brown, then he’s a real player at 170 pounds . Rounding out UFC Halloween’s main card is Ode’ Osbourne vs. Cody Durden , Yana Santos vs. Luana Santos and Jean-Paul Lebosnoyani vs. Farman Hasanov . The “Prelims” are headlined by Francis Marshall vs. Dakota Hope . The biggest match-up on that portion of the card is Zachary Reese vs. Mickey Gall , with Gall looking to avoid his fifth straight loss. Former OKTAGON two-division champ Lucia Szabova also debuts at this event. She fights Tainara Lisboa . The rest of undercard includes Rodrigo Sezinando vs. Theodor Berggren , Julian Erosa vs. Jeong Yeong Lee ( in a retirement fight for Juicy J ), Nick Klein vs. Joseph Kropschott and Talita Alencar vs. Piera Rodriguez . item.title: Moreira on best game ‘so far’ for Milan, while Pulisic is lucky charm against Inter
item.description: Moreira on best game ‘so far’ for Milan, while Pulisic is lucky charm against Inter Diego Moreira admits this was his best Milan performance ‘for now’ after a goal and two assists, while Christian Pulisic jokes about his incredible record against Inter. The Derby della Madonnina was dominated by the Rossoneri, who surged into a 2-0 lead in the opening 10 minutes thanks to the Pulisic header and Adrien Rabiot strike, both on assists from Diego Moreira. The Belgium international secured his Man of the Match status by getting on the scoresheet with a viciously dipping free kick in the 3-1 victory. Diego Moreira and Pulisic relish Milan night ITALY – OCTOBER 31: Diego Moreira of AC Milan celebrates scoring his team’s third goal during the Serie A match between AC Milan and FC Internazionale at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 31, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) “I am very happy, with my teammates we did a great job, we fought to earn the three points,” Moreira told Sky Sport Italia. “We have to stay focused game by game, it’s still early in the season, we need to take it step by step. For now, it is my best game in the Milan shirt. For now.” Check the Football Italia Player Ratings for Milan 3-1 Inter ITALY – OCTOBER 31: Diego Moreira of AC Milan celebrates scoring his team’s third goal during the Serie A match between AC Milan and FC Internazionale at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 31, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Kaka was in the stands and inducted into the Milan Hall of Fame before kick-off, visibly moved to tears as he saluted the crowd. How did Moreira feel scoring in the derby with Kaka watching, wearing the same 22 jersey that the Brazilian had here? “Thank you for coming and giving me your shirt, I am very happy!” ITALY – OCTOBER 31: Christian Pulisic of AC Milan celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the Serie A match between AC Milan and FC Internazionale at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 31, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) This was the first Derby della Madonnina for Diego Moreira, but Pulisic is now an old hand at this fixture and opened the scoring within four minutes. “We started very strong with intensity, physicality, scored two goals and then the third before half-time. This victory is very important for us,” Pulisic told Sky Sport Italia. The American has scored in four editions of the derby and Milan won all of them, so is he their lucky charm? “I want to continue scoring goals in the derby, so that way we’ll win! These are three very important points, but we’ve got to find this consistency to play like this all the time. In the big games, it’s not a surprise that we do well.”

item.title: Steve O'Donnell Shuts Down NASCAR Buyout Speculation Amid Investors Circling Daytona Beach’s Door
item.description: SAN DIEGO, CA – JUNE 21: NASCAR, Motorsport, USA CEO Steve ODonnell during the NASCAR Cup Series Anduril 250 Race the Base event on Sunday June 21, 2026 at the Naval Base Coronado in San Diego, CA. Photo by David J. Griffin/Icon Sportswire AUTO: JUN 21 NASCAR Cup Series Anduril 250 Race the Base EDITORIAL USE ONLY Icon9532606211036 ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire NASCAR has spent nearly eight decades building a business that extends far beyond what happens on the racetrack. Its value stretches across television rights, iconic venues, sponsorships, and a loyal American fan base. With live sports becoming increasingly attractive to investors, the sanctioning body has reasons to draw attention from businesses looking for their next major opportunity. But there is a difference between wanting a piece of NASCAR’s commercial success and convincing the people who own it to surrender control. For the France family, that distinction is particularly important. NASCAR remains a privately held business, and outside interest inevitably raises questions about its long-term ownership. Whether the approaches represent an opportunity to bring fresh capital into the sport or the beginning of another takeover conversation is a different matter altogether. “For its part, the Daytona Beach-based governing body NASCAR has been on the receiving end of unsolicited approaches by businesses seeking equity in the company or to work on joint ventures, according to people familiar with the matter,” reported Sports Business Journal, according to SpeedFreaks . NASCAR CEO Steve O’Donnell has said that NASCAR is not for sale, and just because investors are showing interest does not mean any deal will happen. The distinction between an outright acquisition and an investment is central to the speculation. The reported approaches do not establish that NASCAR has received a formal takeover bid or started a sale process. Instead, they point towards businesses exploring minority ownership opportunities or joint ventures. Both could bring outside money into the organization without necessarily changing who controls it. NASCAR's leadership is drawing a clear line in the sand as major money circles the sport. Subscribe to stay ahead of what's really driving these pivotal negotiations. This is not the first time the France family has faced questions about selling. In 2018, NASCAR reportedly engaged Goldman Sachs to explore potential investment and ownership options. NBCUniversal emerged as a serious prospective buyer, with discussions involving a possible minority stake. However, the proposed transaction never materialized after parent company Comcast shifted its attention towards acquiring Sky. The France family ultimately retained control. item.content:encoded: SAN DIEGO, CA – JUNE 21: NASCAR, Motorsport, USA CEO Steve ODonnell during the NASCAR Cup Series Anduril 250 Race the Base event on Sunday June 21, 2026 at the Naval Base Coronado in San Diego, CA. Photo by David J. Griffin/Icon Sportswire AUTO: JUN 21 NASCAR Cup Series Anduril 250 Race the Base EDITORIAL USE ONLY Icon9532606211036 ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire NASCAR has spent nearly eight decades building a business that extends far beyond what happens on the racetrack. Its value stretches across television rights, iconic venues, sponsorships, and a loyal American fan base. With live sports becoming increasingly attractive to investors, the sanctioning body has reasons to draw attention from businesses looking for their next major opportunity. But there is a difference between wanting a piece of NASCAR’s commercial success and convincing the people who own it to surrender control. For the France family, that distinction is particularly important. NASCAR remains a privately held business, and outside interest inevitably raises questions about its long-term ownership. Whether the approaches represent an opportunity to bring fresh capital into the sport or the beginning of another takeover conversation is a different matter altogether. “For its part, the Daytona Beach-based governing body NASCAR has been on the receiving end of unsolicited approaches by businesses seeking equity in the company or to work on joint ventures, according to people familiar with the matter,” reported Sports Business Journal, according to SpeedFreaks . NASCAR CEO Steve O’Donnell has said that NASCAR is not for sale, and just because investors are showing interest does not mean any deal will happen. The distinction between an outright acquisition and an investment is central to the speculation. The reported approaches do not establish that NASCAR has received a formal takeover bid or started a sale process. Instead, they point towards businesses exploring minority ownership opportunities or joint ventures. Both could bring outside money into the organization without necessarily changing who controls it. NASCAR's leadership is drawing a clear line in the sand as major money circles the sport. Subscribe to stay ahead of what's really driving these pivotal negotiations. This is not the first time the France family has faced questions about selling. In 2018, NASCAR reportedly engaged Goldman Sachs to explore potential investment and ownership options. NBCUniversal emerged as a serious prospective buyer, with discussions involving a possible minority stake. However, the proposed transaction never materialized after parent company Comcast shifted its attention towards acquiring Sky. The France family ultimately retained control. The renewed interest is understandable when NASCAR’s commercial position is considered. Its seven-year media rights agreements, running from 2025 through 2031, involve FOX, NBC, Amazon’s Prime Video, and TNT Sports. The reported value of the Cup Series and Xfinity Series agreements is approximately $7.7 billion, providing a substantial long-term revenue foundation. Few American sports properties can offer investors that kind of established broadcasting business. NASCAR also has an important advantage in its ownership of a significant portfolio of racing venues. Its 2019 acquisition of International Speedway Corporation brought the two businesses together, giving NASCAR greater control over its tracks and the commercial opportunities surrounding them. Beyond race-day ticket sales, those properties offer potential for hospitality, entertainment, real estate development, and other events. An investor interested in unlocking that value might prefer a joint venture over purchasing the entire organization. There is another reason outside capital could appeal to NASCAR. Private equity has already found its way into the team ownership landscape. Trackhouse Racing, for instance, brought in Avenue Sports Fund, led by former Milwaukee Bucks co-owner Marc Lasry, through a significant minority investment in 2024. That transaction demonstrated the appetite for motorsports investments, although buying into a racing team is fundamentally different from acquiring an interest in the sanctioning body. The financial case for accepting an investor is therefore straightforward. NASCAR could unlock some of its considerable enterprise value while bringing in capital to strengthen its international presence, improve digital distribution, and develop its commercial properties. A strategic partner could also provide expertise in areas where the sport has room to grow. The France family would potentially benefit financially without necessarily relinquishing control. However, selling would introduce complications that go beyond ownership percentages. NASCAR’s relationship with its teams has been under considerable strain, particularly following the antitrust dispute involving 23XI Racing and Front Row Motorsports. The December 2025 settlement introduced evergreen charters and ended a prolonged legal battle over the sport’s commercial structure. Although the agreement provided greater long-term security for teams, its financial terms remained confidential. Any prospective investor would inherit those relationships and the responsibility of maintaining a sustainable business for all stakeholders. Formula One offers a useful comparison. Liberty Media completed its acquisition of the championship in 2017, in a transaction valuing the business at approximately $8 billion. Under its ownership, F1 placed greater emphasis on digital engagement, social media, international expansion, and reaching younger audiences. Netflix’s Drive to Survive subsequently helped introduce the championship to a broader American audience. The transformation demonstrated how a new ownership group could approach motorsports as a global entertainment property rather than simply a racing championship. But NASCAR cannot simply replicate that model. Formula One operates on a global calendar, while NASCAR’s identity and commercial strength remain deeply connected to the American market. Liberty’s investment also does not establish that a sale would automatically deliver similar results for NASCAR. A new controlling owner could bring fresh ideas, but pressure to maximize returns might also influence decisions involving ticket prices, scheduling, venue development, and the sport’s relationship with its teams. That is ultimately what makes O’Donnell’s position important. NASCAR can entertain investment proposals, explore commercial partnerships, and assess opportunities without putting the entire organization on the market. Investor interest is not the same as an acquisition agreement, and the France family has little reason to surrender control simply because outside businesses see potential in the sport. The question is no longer whether NASCAR is valuable enough to attract serious investment. Its media contracts, venues, and commercial reach have already established that. The bigger question is whether outside capital can make the sport more valuable without compromising the control and independence the France family has maintained since 1948. For now, O’Donnell’s message leaves little room for interpreting investor interest as an indication that NASCAR is preparing to sell. SHOP: Ohio State vs. Oregon college football tickets The No. 2-ranked team won a thriller last week against No. 4 Indiana; however, they lost quarterback Julian Sayin to an arm injury that could keep him out the remainder of the regular season. item.title: Kane Misses Penalty After Ballon d’Or Feat As Bayern Held By Dortmund
item.description: Fabio Silva’s 89th-minute goal earned Borussia Dortmund a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich after Harry Kane missed a penalty in a see-saw Bundesliga clash on Saturday. Bayern were 1-0 up when Kane, playing his first match since winning the Ballon d’Or on Monday, rattled his second-half spot kick against the crossbar. Dortmund’s Serhou Guirassy levelled shortly after, but Kane helped Bayern retake the lead when he set up a Dayot Upamecano goal. In the final minute, substitutes Konstantinos Karetsas and Silva combined to grab Dortmund a share of the spoils. “Coming back twice here in Munich is no easy feat. We earned a well-deserved point here today,” Dortmund coach Niko Kovac told Sky Germany, adding his side “never stopped believing in ourselves.” Dortmund’s Guinean forward #09 Serhou Guirassy (C) scores the 1-1 goal during the German first division Bundesliga football match between FC Bayern Munich and BVB Borussia Dortmund in Munich, southern Germany, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Alexandra BEIER / AFP) The result leaves the two sides level atop the Bundesliga table, with defending champions Bayern ahead on goal difference. It is just the fourth time in the past 18 ‘Klassiker’ matches that Bayern have not emerged victorious. In addition to the late draw, Bayern, who are without Vincent Kompany as he recovers from a virus, will be concerned by further injuries to their undermanned forward line ahead of Tuesday’s trip to Atletico Madrid. Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry and Michael Olise were all subbed out on Saturday, with Jamal Musiala and Luis Diaz already out with injury. Bayern sporting director Max Eberl said the draw appeared “costly”, with Saibari and Gnabry’s injuries “somewhat serious”. Bayern captain Joshua Kimmich, who returned after missing three matches after the sudden death of his father, said: “It’s been a really, really hard week, but you can forget during the game. “Other than the result today, you have to say we’re going through difficult moments right now, now with the injuries we picked up.” Kane was honoured pre-match with his Ballon d’Or shown to the Bayern faithful for the first time. Bayern Munich’s English forward Harry Kane shows his Ballon d’Or trophy to the fans prior to the German first division Bundesliga football match between FC Bayern Munich and BVB Borussia Dortmund in Munich, southern Germany, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Alexandra BEIER / AFP) Dortmund thought they had taken the lead with 35 minutes gone as Jobe Bellingham scored from close range, but VAR overturned the goal for offside. Bayern made Dortmund pay immediately when Konrad Laimer pounced on a poor Felix Nmecha pass and charged upfield to score. Bayern were better after the break and a Nmecha handball brought Kane to the spot, but the England captain rifled his shot against the crossbar. Moments later, Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck intercepted a Kane pass, thundered up the pitch and found Carney Chukwuemeka, who laid off for Guirassy to score at th

We earned a well-deserved point here today,” Dortmund coach Niko Kovac told Sky Germany, adding his side “never stopped believing in ourselves.” Dortmund’s Guinean forward #09 Serhou Guirassy (C) scores the 1-1 goal during the German first division Bundesliga football match between FC Bayern Munich and BVB Borussia Dortmund in Munich, southern Germany, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Alexandra BEIER / AFP) The result leaves the two sides level atop the Bundesliga table, with defending champions Bayern ahead on goal difference. It is just the fourth time in the past 18 ‘Klassiker’ matches that Bayern have not emerged victorious. In addition to the late draw, Bayern, who are without Vincent Kompany as he recovers from a virus, will be concerned by further injuries to their undermanned forward line ahead of Tuesday’s trip to Atletico Madrid. Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry and Michael Olise were all subbed out on Saturday, with Jamal Musiala and Luis Diaz already out with injury. Bayern sporting director Max Eberl said the draw appeared “costly”, with Saibari and Gnabry’s injuries “somewhat serious”. Bayern captain Joshua Kimmich, who returned after missing three matches after the sudden death of his father, said: “It’s been a really, really hard week, but you can forget during the game. “Other than the result today, you have to say we’re going through difficult moments right now, now with the injuries we picked up.” Kane was honoured pre-match with his Ballon d’Or shown to the Bayern faithful for the first time. Bayern Munich’s English forward Harry Kane shows his Ballon d’Or trophy to the fans prior to the German first division Bundesliga football match between FC Bayern Munich and BVB Borussia Dortmund in Munich, southern Germany, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Alexandra BEIER / AFP) Dortmund thought they had taken the lead with 35 minutes gone as Jobe Bellingham scored from close range, but VAR overturned the goal for offside. Bayern made Dortmund pay immediately when Konrad Laimer pounced on a poor Felix Nmecha pass and charged upfield to score. Bayern were better after the break and a Nmecha handball brought Kane to the spot, but the England captain rifled his shot against the crossbar. Moments later, Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck intercepted a Kane pass, thundered up the pitch and found Carney Chukwuemeka, who laid off for Guirassy to score at the near post. Kane looked to have redeemed himself when he set up a goal for Upamecano, but Silva levelled in the dying stages. Fuellkrug’s Fine Form Werder Bremen striker Niclas Fuellkrug continued his remarkable scoring run since returning on a season-long loan from West Ham, grabbing the opener in a 2-0 win over Hoffenheim. Eren Dinkci also scored for Bremen, but the 33-year-old Fuellkrug was the story again. By scoring in his seventh consecutive Bundesliga start, he equalled Rudi Voeller’s club record from 1982-83. “I don’t score these goals to break records,” Fuellkrug said, but added the mark was “nice”. “It’s an absolute joy to play with this group.” He has 12 goals in 10 matches in all competitions for Bremen this season, after scoring just three goals in 18 months at West Ham and one at AC Milan during a six-month loan. RB Leipzig won 2-0 at promoted Schalke to pick up their first away points this season. Antonio Nusa opened the scoring with a penalty after 37 minutes, and Romulo scored 12 minutes from time to sink the hosts. Leipzig, who welcome Manchester City in the Champions League on Wednesday, had won all four of their home Bundesliga matches by an 18-0 aggregate but had lost all three of their away games this season. The victory took Leipzig to fourth, one point behind third-placed Freiburg, who came from behind to win 2-1 at Augsburg. Ermedin Demirovic scored twice as Stuttgart broke out of a funk to win 4-2 away at in-form Bayer Leverkusen. Jamie Leweling and Bilal El Khannouss also scored for Stuttgart, who had won just three of their previous eight matches. AFP The post Kane Misses Penalty After Ballon d’Or Feat As Bayern Held By Dortmund appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Every Resident Evil Game, Ranked From Worst to Best
item.description: After decades of misses, 2026 gave us one of the best gaming adaptations of all time. Well, sort of. Zach Cregger’s take on Resident Evil was a hit among critics who have praised the horror movie for its delightfully playful tone. The only catch is that it didn't have much to do with the established lore and characters of the actual Resident Evil games . Instead, it told its own story in the universe, which is probably for the better, considering how complicated the game saga gets.

item.title: Clashes Erupt In France As Thousands Protest Cost Of Living, Inequality
item.description: A police officer in Paris was injured after being struck by a Molotov cocktail as clashes erupted in the capital and other cities during protests across France against soaring living costs and inequality. Hundreds of thousands of people, some dressed for Halloween, demonstrated across France in a third consecutive weekend of largely peaceful demonstrations. But the Paris police prefecture said that several hundred rioters had attacked security forces with projectiles, including a Molotov cocktail. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez pointed to an “extraordinary” level of violence from some, blaming far-left extremist groups for attacks on security forces. He described the throwing of a Molotov cocktail at a riot police officer in Paris as an “attempted murder,” adding that the officer had escaped with minor injuries. “We are fully prepared for those looking for confrontation tonight,” he added. After a march on the outskirts of Paris in bright sunshine, clashes broke out between police and some demonstrators as the procession reached its final destination. Dozens of masked people dressed in black used hammers to pry up paving stones and hurl them at police, AFP journalists saw. Police responded with tear gas and several baton charges. ‘Engulfed In Flames’ Far-right leader Marine Le Pen said those responsible for the Molotov attack must be “punished with the utmost severity.” “The images of a police officer engulfed in flames after being targeted with incendiary devices are unbearable,” Le Pen said on X. A French riot gendarme mobile has flames rising up his uniform after being hit by a Molotov cocktail during a charge against demonstrators at the end of a demonstration part of a nationwide day of protests over the rising cost of living and inequality organised by Yellow Vest movement, labour unions and high school and university students organisations, in Paris on October 31, 2026. Photo by SAMEER AL-DOUMY / AFP A night-time curfew was to be imposed in the central Paris Republique and Chatelet-Les Halles neighbourhoods from 11:00 pm to 6:00 am on Saturday and Sunday. Police arrested more than 420 people across the country. The interior ministry said that “radical elements” in cities including Bordeaux, Toulouse and Marseille had attempted to enter city centres “with the aim of carrying out vandalism and looting”. In Lyon, France’s third-largest city, people threw projectiles at police, prompting officers to fire tear gas. In the southern city of Toulouse, police used water cannon against an unauthorised protest that drew several thousand people. ‘Attack On Freedom’ Earlier Saturday, thousands of people, some wearing costumes ranging from Spider-Man to Frankenstein, marched through eastern Paris as a helicopter circled overhead. item.content:encoded: A police officer in Paris was injured after being struck by a Molotov cocktail as clashes erupted in the capital and other cities during protests across France against soaring living costs and inequality. Hundreds of thousands of people, some dressed for Halloween, demonstrated across France in a third consecutive weekend of largely peaceful demonstrations. But the Paris police prefecture said that several hundred rioters had attacked security forces with projectiles, including a Molotov cocktail. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez pointed to an “extraordinary” level of violence from some, blaming far-left extremist groups for attacks on security forces. He described the throwing of a Molotov cocktail at a riot police officer in Paris as an “attempted murder,” adding that the officer had escaped with minor injuries. “We are fully prepared for those looking for confrontation tonight,” he added. After a march on the outskirts of Paris in bright sunshine, clashes broke out between police and some demonstrators as the procession reached its final destination. Dozens of masked people dressed in black used hammers to pry up paving stones and hurl them at police, AFP journalists saw. Police responded with tear gas and several baton charges. ‘Engulfed In Flames’ Far-right leader Marine Le Pen said those responsible for the Molotov attack must be “punished with the utmost severity.” “The images of a police officer engulfed in flames after being targeted with incendiary devices are unbearable,” Le Pen said on X. A French riot gendarme mobile has flames rising up his uniform after being hit by a Molotov cocktail during a charge against demonstrators at the end of a demonstration part of a nationwide day of protests over the rising cost of living and inequality organised by Yellow Vest movement, labour unions and high school and university students organisations, in Paris on October 31, 2026. Photo by SAMEER AL-DOUMY / AFP A night-time curfew was to be imposed in the central Paris Republique and Chatelet-Les Halles neighbourhoods from 11:00 pm to 6:00 am on Saturday and Sunday. Police arrested more than 420 people across the country. The interior ministry said that “radical elements” in cities including Bordeaux, Toulouse and Marseille had attempted to enter city centres “with the aim of carrying out vandalism and looting”. In Lyon, France’s third-largest city, people threw projectiles at police, prompting officers to fire tear gas. In the southern city of Toulouse, police used water cannon against an unauthorised protest that drew several thousand people. ‘Attack On Freedom’ Earlier Saturday, thousands of people, some wearing costumes ranging from Spider-Man to Frankenstein, marched through eastern Paris as a helicopter circled overhead. Placards read: “No need for tear gas to make our future look bleak” and “Dressed up as an angry citizen for Halloween.” “The fact that demonstrations are being pushed outside city centres, and that so many protests are being banned, is really an attack on freedom,” said Alice Hien, a video game developer. Authorities said that some 320,000 people rallied across France including 70,000 in Paris. According to youth organisations, nearly half a million people demonstrated, including 200,000 in the capital. Elections Looming The demonstrations come in a febrile political climate, with presidential elections less than six months away and Le Pen topping opinion polls. The protest movement, bringing together Yellow Vest activists, trade unions, and high school and university students, initially focused on the rising cost of living, inequality, and deteriorating learning conditions. Following a security clampdown and serious injuries to some protesters, the movement broadened its demands to include greater protection of civil liberties and the right to protest. In the northern French city of Lille, 47-year-old Aurelie Herrmann danced at the protest. “I dance because on television they only show damage and destruction, whereas you can perfectly well demonstrate in good spirits,” she said. New School Blockades Student protesters complained the police had not authorised a march through the centre of the French capital and vowed to stage new blockades of high schools and universities next week. “Starting this Tuesday, we will blockade our universities and high schools, and we will do so again on Thursday before joining the demonstration on November 5 called by workers and trade unions,” said Sabrine Kharbach, spokeswoman for the Union Etudiante (Student Union). Ahead of the protests, some shopkeepers barricaded their businesses. With the eurozone’s second-largest economy on the brink of recession and under pressure to rein in its debt, the government has limited scope to appease protesters through additional spending.
