item.title: German Police, Protesters Clash After ‘Gen Z’ Protest, Several Police Officers Injured
item.description: German police and protesters clashed across the country Saturday following massive youth-led protests, with authorities using water cannon and pepper spray as masked demonstrators hurled fireworks, stones and bottles. Several police officers were injured in the violence after tens of thousands joined protests nationwide that were organised by the group “GenZ regelt!” (Gen Z has got this!). The demonstrations, inspired by similar movements in France and Italy calling for political elites to heed the concerns of the younger generation, were largely peaceful during the day. But tensions peaked in the evening as some groups of protesters refused to disperse. Police were pelted with projectiles in the western city of Frankfurt, and responded by using water cannon and pepper spray as they sought to clear protesters. “Incidents of stones and fireworks being thrown at the emergency services continue to occur,” police said on X. “We are taking action against these troublemakers.” Police also used water cannon in the cities of Hamburg and Cologne after they said demonstrators targeted emergency service workers with fireworks, stones and bottles. ‘Boiling Point’ In Berlin, a protest that was not organised by the “GenZ regelt!” movement took place in the evening, with police reporting they were pelted with eggs and bottles. Police in the eastern city of Leipzig also used pepper spray after protests turned violent while a police officer in Bonn suffered minor injuries during a confrontation with a group. Police were reported to have made several arrests. Police detain a protester after a demonstration organised by “GenZ regelt!” Photo by RALF HIRSCHBERGER / AFP The youth-led protests earlier in the day took place in a mostly peaceful and festive atmosphere, with some dressed in outfits ranging from dinosaurs to Batman as the demonstrations coincided with Halloween.They waved signs that read “Time for resistance”, and “Merz must go”, in reference to conservative Chancellor Friedrich Merz. “I think it’s really important to show solidarity with all the other protests currently happening across Europe, including in France,” Milla, a 20-year-old student who only gave her first name, told AFP in Berlin. “I’ve been waiting for a long time for something to finally really happen, and for people to tackle this with a bit more force. I believe that today here is the first step.” Marius, a 23-year-old care worker, added that “politicians need to know about this… the situation is slowly reaching boiling point.” “I think we can all feel that this just isn’t working anymore,” he added. The movement’s complaints range from the high cost of living to poorly maintained schools, government spending cuts and, more broadly, what it sees as politicians making decisions with apparently little regard for the younger generation. But tensions peaked in the evening as some groups of protesters refused to disperse. Police in the eastern city of Leipzig also used pepper spray after protests turned violent while a police officer in Bonn suffered minor injuries during a confrontation with a group. Police were reported to have made several arrests. Police detain a protester after a demonstration organised by “GenZ regelt!” Photo by RALF HIRSCHBERGER / AFP The youth-led protests earlier in the day took place in a mostly peaceful and festive atmosphere, with some dressed in outfits ranging from dinosaurs to Batman as the demonstrations coincided with Halloween.They waved signs that read “Time for resistance”, and “Merz must go”, in reference to conservative Chancellor Friedrich Merz. “I think it’s really important to show solidarity with all the other protests currently happening across Europe, including in France,” Milla, a 20-year-old student who only gave her first name, told AFP in Berlin. “I’ve been waiting for a long time for something to finally really happen, and for people to tackle this with a bit more force. I believe that today here is the first step.” Marius, a 23-year-old care worker, added that “politicians need to know about this… the situation is slowly reaching boiling point.” “I think we can all feel that this just isn’t working anymore,” he added. The movement’s complaints range from the high cost of living to poorly maintained schools, government spending cuts and, more broadly, what it sees as politicians making decisions with apparently little regard for the younger generation. They are also unhappy with sharply increased military spending and a new voluntary service model aimed at boosting troop numbers, fearing it is a step towards bringing back conscription. Europe-Wide Protests “GenZ regelt!” said some 120,000 people took part in the demonstrations. Police said the main protests themselves had been “very peaceful”. When violence broke out in the evening, police “intervened very decisively and also forcefully”, Andreas Rosskopf, an official from the police union, told the Rheinische Post daily. He also noted that major property damage had so far been avoided. Some jewellery stores and luxury clothing shops boarded up their windows ahead of the protests to ward off looters. Protests also took place in France Saturday for a third straight weekend, with clashes erupting in Paris and elsewhere. Nationwide demonstrations there on October 17 degenerated into some of the country’s worst rioting in years. Berlin has been in contact with officials in France and Italy amid fears that radicals from overseas could seek to join the German protests. The “GenZ regelt!” movement explicitly rejected violence. It said that “extremist groups, anti-constitutional symbols, racism and hate speech have no place with us — no matter from which side.” AFP The post German Police, Protesters Clash After ‘Gen Z’ Protest, Several Police Officers Injured appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Binance says has covered 90% of $6.3 billion hack losses
item.description: Cryptocurrency platform Binance said Saturday it has used company money to buy tokens to replenish 90 percent of $6.3 billion stolen in a huge hacking attack. “Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident,” the company said on X. Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes, said the remaining 10 percent of tokens are “less liquid, which means they may take longer to source in the required amounts.” The company said it has set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses in the hack. Binance said Friday it was working to resolve what it called a “complex attack” with several “points of breach.” Investigators pointed to hackers linked to North Korea as being responsible. The prices of most major cryptocurrencies fell on news of the cyberattack. Binance suspended user withdrawals after the incident, but said in its latest update they were on track to resume Sunday. The attack on Binance came as many observers express worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols. President Donald Trump said Friday the United States was looking into the hack, and the FBI said it was “engaged with relevant public and private partners to understand the scope of the activity” and was ready to investigate. The post Binance says has covered 90% of $6.3 billion hack losses appeared first on Vanguard News .

President Donald Trump said Friday the United States was looking into the hack, and the FBI said it was “engaged with relevant public and private partners to understand the scope of the activity” and was ready to investigate. item.title: Insecurity didn’t begin in Tinubu’s administration – Dogara
item.description: A former Speaker of the House of Representatives, Mr Yakubu Dogara, says Nigeria’s security challenges predate the administration of President Bola Tinubu. Dogara, who is the Chancellor of Achievers University, Owo, Ondo State, made the assertion at the institution’s 16th convocation ceremony, where 836 graduands received various academic qualifications. He said terrorism, insurgency, banditry, kidnapping and communal violence had been entrenched in the country long before the current administration assumed office in May 2023. According to him, the nation’s security problems are rooted in years of porous borders, illegal arms proliferation, high youth unemployment and the spread of extremist ideologies. “Insecurity in Nigeria did not begin with this administration. This is no excuse, because the facts need no defence. Terrorism, insurgency, banditry, kidnapping and communal violence did not arrive in 2023,” Dogara said. He explained that the security situation developed over several years, stressing that its roots went deep long before the current government took over. Dogara, however, noted that President Tinubu had consistently identified national security as a top priority and major responsibility of his administration. The chancellor charged the graduands to deploy their talents, creativity and innovation toward national development. Speaking, the Pro-Chancellor of the university, Prof. Bode Ayorinde, acknowledged the progress made in expanding access to tertiary education, but expressed concern over the job prospects of graduates. Ayorinde cited figures from the National Universities Commission (NUC), which put the number of universities in Nigeria at 312 as of June 2026, comprising 77 federal, 67 state-owned, and 168 private institutions. He said although the growth represented a huge investment in human capital by parents, governments and lecturers, deliberate efforts must be made to create viable opportunities for graduates after school. In her address, the Vice-Chancellor of the institution, Prof. Omolola Irinoye, reiterated the university’s commitment to providing quality education that combines intellectual growth, practical skills, character building and social responsibility. Irinoye said that there were 98 First Class graduates in the academic session, attributing the performance to the institution’s investment in quality assurance, staff development and a conducive learning environment. According to her, the university also operates flexible payment arrangements to accommodate students from different socioeconomic backgrounds. “The institution’s scholarship programme was designed to ensure that financial constraints did not prevent deserving students from acquiring university education. “The university has 100 per cent tuition scholarship in 17 academic programmes, with 80 per cent tuition scholarship in five academic programmes while there were also 70 per cent tuition scholarship in other five academic programmes,” she said. item.title: 'Adolescence' Creator Officially Confirms a Connection Between His Netflix and Apple Shows
item.description: Co-created by Stephen Graham and Jack Thorne, the 2025 British limited series Adolescence made waves worldwide when it debuted on Netflix. Adolescence explores the immediate fallout from a young boy, Jamie (Owen Cooper), stabbing a girl to death and the radicalization of men online. The series was so well received that a UK government–backed initiative made it free to watch in high schools.

item.title: Naderi breaks Aberdeen’s resistance as Rangers reach Premier Sports Cup final
item.description: Ryan Naderi’s dramatic late strike broke down Aberdeen’s stubborn resistance to earn Rangers a place in the Premier Sports Cup final. Aberdeen restricted Rangers to one shot on target in a low quality first half, but Derek McInnes’s side picked up the pace after the break. Aberdeen survived relentless pressure at times but in the 83rd minute, Naderi redirected a strike from James Penrice into the net for his eight goal of the season to seal a 1-0 win at Hampden Park. item.title: Katsina Debunks Campaign Violence Claims, Orders Probe Into Yankara Incident
item.description: The Katsina State Government has dismissed reports linking the incident that occurred in Yankara, Faskari Local Government Area, to Governor Dikko Radda’s Tinubu-Dikko 2027 campaign, describing such claims as false and misleading. In a statement, the government said preliminary findings showed that the disturbance stemmed from a disagreement between participants in a Maulud procession and security personnel over designated procession routes, resulting in confusion along a public street in Yankara. It stressed that the incident was entirely unrelated to thegovernor’s campaign activities or the Tinubu-Dikko campaign rally held in Faskari. According to the government, Governor Radda passed through Yankara without incident on his way to Faskari, where he paid a courtesy visit to the District Head’s Palace and was received by the district head and other traditional rulers. The governor, it said, later proceeded to the Faskari Local Government secretariat, where he inspected ongoing renovation works at the secretariat and council chambers before attending the campaign rally and interacting with residents and supporters. Governor Dikko Radda addresses a crowd of supporters at the Tinubu-Dikko 2027 campaign in Faskari Local Government Area of Katsina State on October 31, 2026. The state government urged relevant security agencies to carry out a thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and ensure that those responsible are identified where necessary. In the statement signed by the Chief Press Secretary to the Governor, Ibrahim Mohammed, the government appealed to residents to remain calm, uphold peace, and avoid spreading unverified information capable of causing unnecessary tension. Violence was reported in Yankara town on Saturday after suspected hoodlums attacked supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC), leaving several people injured and a campaign vehicle set ablaze. Eyewitnesses said the attackers allegedly ambushed APC supporters heading to Governor Radda’s campaign rally in Faskari, disrupting movement along the major road and causing panic among residents. Angry youths were also alleged to have blocked the route the campaign convoy was expected to use. The post Katsina Debunks Campaign Violence Claims, Orders Probe Into Yankara Incident appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Kane misses penalty as Bayern held by Dortmund
item.description: Fabio Silva’s 89th-minute goal earned Borussia Dortmund a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich after Harry Kane missed a penalty in a see-saw Bundesliga clash on Saturday. Read Also: How Kane edged Mbappe to Ballon d’Or win Bayern were 1-0 up when Kane, playing his first match since winning the Ballon d’Or on Monday, rattled his second-half spot kick against the crossbar. Dortmund’s Serhou Guirassy levelled things up shortly after, but Kane helped Bayern retake the lead when he set up a Dayot Upamecano goal. But in the final minute, substitutes Konstantinos Karetsas and Silva combined to grab Dortmund a share of the spoils. The result leaves the two ‘Der Klassiker’ sides level on points atop the Bundesliga table, with defending champions Bayern ahead on goal difference. It is just the fourth time in the past 18 matches between these sides that Bayern have not emerged victorious. In addition to the late draw, Bayern, who are without Vincent Kompany as he recovers from a virus, will be concerned by further injuries to their undermanned forward line ahead of Tuesday’s trip to Atletico Madrid. Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry and Michael Olise were all subbed out on Saturday, with Jamal Musiala and Luis Diaz already out with injury. Kane was honoured pre-match with his Ballon d’Or shown to the Bayern faithful for the first time. Dortmund thought they had taken the lead with 35 minutes gone as Jobe Bellingham scored from close range, but VAR overturned the goal for offside. Bayern made Dortmund pay immediately when Konrad Laimer pounced on a poor Felix Nmecha pass and charged upfield to score. Bayern were better after the break and a Nmecha handball brought Kane to the spot, but the normally reliable England captain rifled his shot against the crossbar. Moments later, Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck thundered up the pitch and found Chukwuemeka, who laid off for Guirassy to score at the near post. Kane looked to have redeemed himself when he set up a goal for Upamecano soon after, but Silva levelled things up once more in the dying stages. Fuellkrug’s fine form Werder Bremen striker Niclas Fuellkrug continued his remarkable scoring run since returning on a season-long loan from West Ham, grabbing the opener in a 2-0 win over Hoffenheim. Eren Dinkci also scored for Bremen but the 33-year-old Fuellkrug was the story again. By scoring in his seventh consecutive Bundesliga start, he equalled Rudi Voeller’s club record from 1982-83. “I don’t score these goals to break records,” Fuellkrug said, but added the mark was “nice”. “It’s an absolute joy to play with this group.” He has 12 goals in 10 matches in all competitions for Bremen this season, after scoring just three goals in 18 months at West Ham and one at AC Milan during a six-month loan. item.title: FG deploys experts to Ogun over recurring gas emissions in schools
item.description: By James Ogunnaike The Federal Government has deployed a specialised technical team to Ogun State to investigate recurring subsurface gas emissions that have triggered health concerns and disrupted academic activities in secondary schools across the Ijebu axis. The intervention, coordinated by the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), is aimed at establishing the geological source of the emissions and recommending lasting solutions to the recurring incidents affecting schools and surrounding communities. The deployment followed reports of localised gas seepages suspected to have caused oxygen depletion and breathing difficulties among students and other residents in the affected communities. Speaking during a joint press briefing and commencement of a site assessment in Ijebu Ode on Saturday, the Federal Government’s Ad-hoc Committee said preliminary indications suggested that the emissions could be associated with natural subsurface geological processes rather than leaks from petroleum pipelines. The team, however, stressed the need for further technical investigations to establish the actual source and nature of the emissions. Speaking at the briefing, the team leader and Assistant Director at the NUPRC, Prosper Okonedo, said the Commission had constituted the committee following an initial assessment conducted by the Ogun State Government. Okonedo explained that the Commission’s Chief Executive, Mrs Oritsemeyawa Eyesan, directed the deployment of experts from its Lagos regional office to collaborate with the state government and investigate the situation. According to him, “about two weeks ago, the Commission Chief Executive of NUPRC, Mrs. Oritsemeyawa Eyesan, advised that we set up an ad-hoc committee from the Lagos regional office to come to the state because the state government had conducted an initial assessment and submitted their report.” He disclosed that the Commission had also been investigating similar incidents in other parts of the country, including communities in Rivers and Delta states. “Presently, we have a study group known as the Epe Study Group. They are looking into similar issues in a village community in Rivers State, and there is one right now in Delta State where we have established that gas seepage is emanating from the subsurface. “However, for this state, we cannot really say what it is right now. That is why we are here, and we are going to deploy to the site to see the situation for ourselves, even though the state government had reported seepages of gas affecting certain secondary schools in some communities,” he said. Okonedo said the federal government was committed to working with the Ogun State government to address the situation and safeguard residents. “The government is there to ensure the welfare and well-being of the Nigerian people. item.dc:creator: Henry Oduah
item.content:encoded: By James Ogunnaike The Federal Government has deployed a specialised technical team to Ogun State to investigate recurring subsurface gas emissions that have triggered health concerns and disrupted academic activities in secondary schools across the Ijebu axis. The intervention, coordinated by the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), is aimed at establishing the geological source of the emissions and recommending lasting solutions to the recurring incidents affecting schools and surrounding communities. The deployment followed reports of localised gas seepages suspected to have caused oxygen depletion and breathing difficulties among students and other residents in the affected communities. Speaking during a joint press briefing and commencement of a site assessment in Ijebu Ode on Saturday, the Federal Government’s Ad-hoc Committee said preliminary indications suggested that the emissions could be associated with natural subsurface geological processes rather than leaks from petroleum pipelines. The team, however, stressed the need for further technical investigations to establish the actual source and nature of the emissions. Speaking at the briefing, the team leader and Assistant Director at the NUPRC, Prosper Okonedo, said the Commission had constituted the committee following an initial assessment conducted by the Ogun State Government. Okonedo explained that the Commission’s Chief Executive, Mrs Oritsemeyawa Eyesan, directed the deployment of experts from its Lagos regional office to collaborate with the state government and investigate the situation. According to him, “about two weeks ago, the Commission Chief Executive of NUPRC, Mrs. Oritsemeyawa Eyesan, advised that we set up an ad-hoc committee from the Lagos regional office to come to the state because the state government had conducted an initial assessment and submitted their report.” He disclosed that the Commission had also been investigating similar incidents in other parts of the country, including communities in Rivers and Delta states. “Presently, we have a study group known as the Epe Study Group. They are looking into similar issues in a village community in Rivers State, and there is one right now in Delta State where we have established that gas seepage is emanating from the subsurface. “However, for this state, we cannot really say what it is right now. That is why we are here, and we are going to deploy to the site to see the situation for ourselves, even though the state government had reported seepages of gas affecting certain secondary schools in some communities,” he said. Okonedo said the federal government was committed to working with the Ogun State government to address the situation and safeguard residents. “The government is there to ensure the welfare and well-being of the Nigerian people. If that is the paramount role of government, that is why we as a Commission have come to work with the state government to proffer solutions to whatever problem exists in this community. “My team and I will do an assessment and come up with a report that will work well for the Nigerian people,” he added. Also speaking, the Ogun State Commissioner for Environment, Mr Ola Oresanya, described the recurring emissions as an emerging environmental challenge that requires coordinated intervention and technical expertise at the national level. Oresanya said similar incidents had been reported in Rivers, Delta and Osun states, suggesting that the problem might extend beyond isolated communities in Ogun. “We have similar problems going on right now in Rivers, Delta, Osun, and here in Ogun State. Coincidentally for us in Ogun State, this is happening around schools. But we need to establish that what is happening around the region is similar to what we are witnessing here; it is not just a local problem,” he said. The commissioner appealed to residents to remain calm while investigations continued, assuring them that the state government was working with relevant experts to determine the cause of the emissions. “All I want to say is that we don’t have any reason to panic. All we need to do is stay concerned, but please don’t panic. What we know and what we are bringing to the table is that the gas affecting our people is subsurface gas. We’ve proved that over and over. “There is no gas pipeline at Owode in Ikenne, and there is no gas pipeline around Ijebu-Omu where these things are happening. It is coming from the upper crust. It is a natural occurrence, and what triggers it will be established,” Oresanya stated. He also ruled out any immediate plan to relocate residents of the affected communities, noting that the government was consulting global practices and examining appropriate public health management measures. Meanwhile, Professor Philip Ikhiane, a Professor of Sedimentary Petroleum Geochemistry at Olabisi Onabanjo University (OOU), Ago-Iwoye, and leader of the Ogun State Technical Investigating Team, disclosed that preliminary geological investigations had identified underground structural features that could be linked to the gas emissions. Ikhiane explained that geological surveys and remote sensing operations had revealed subsurface lineaments, which could represent faults, fractures or joints beneath the affected areas. According to him, these geological structures could provide pathways through which naturally occurring gases migrate from underground formations to the surface. He said further investigations would be required to establish the relationship between the identified geological features and the reported emissions. The latest intervention comes amid growing concerns following repeated incidents in which more than 100 students from secondary schools in Ijebu-Ode, Ago-Iwoye and Ijebu-Igbo were reportedly hospitalised after inhaling an offensive gaseous substance. The affected students were taken to the State Hospital, Ijebu-Ode, General Hospital, Ijebu-Igbo, and other healthcare facilities for medical attention. Among the schools reportedly worst affected are Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School, Anglican Girls Grammar School, Ijebu-Ode, and Itamerin Comprehensive High School, Ago-Iwoye. A video circulating on social media showed some students collapsing and being rushed to hospitals following the suspected exposure. The Ogun State Government had earlier identified the substance as methane, although the Federal Government’s latest investigation is expected to establish the precise source, composition and geological pathway of the emissions. A teacher in one of the affected schools, who spoke on condition of anonymity, described the incident as frightening, saying students and members of staff suddenly developed breathing difficulties. “The incident happened at about 10 am. The students and the staff started inhaling this gas and began to have difficulty in breathing and were fainting, after which they were rushed to the hospitals,” the teacher said. Saturday’s intervention is coming against the backdrop of a series of similar incidents that have heightened anxiety among parents, teachers and residents across Ijebu land. The first reported incident occurred in April, affecting about 40 students. In May, more than 120 students were reportedly hospitalised following another exposure, while a further 69 students were taken to hospitals on June 1 after another occurrence. Schools previously affected include Our Lady of Apostles Secondary School, Epe Garage, Ijebu-Ode; Anglican Girls Grammar School, Ijebu-Ode; and St Anthony Grammar School, Ijebu-Imusin. The recurring incidents have raised concerns about the safety of students and staff in the affected schools, as well as the possible long-term environmental and public health implications for surrounding communities. item.title: If Mikel Arteta’s dossier is part of a deliberate strategy, it is a dangerous one for Arsenal | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The manager is not yet in Alex Ferguson and José Mourinho’s league, but his conspiracy theories have reached new levels English football loves the word “dossier”. It doesn’t love dossiers themselves, of course; they’re for nerds – unless, that is, they’re a “secret dossier”, which have a thrilling redolence of spy dramas, invisible ink and dead drops. Non-secret dossiers, though, are inherently risible: call something a “dossier” in English football and you’re immediately signalling: this is absurd poindextering. Dossiers were preposterous when Don Revie was – imagine the pretension! – drawing up scouting reports on opposing players, and they are preposterous today as Mikel Arteta collates images of rival managers stepping outside their technical area. Arteta, it should be said, did not use the word “dossier”; rather it was swiftly applied to what he had called “a massive storage of images”. During Arsenal’s 2-0 win against Everton last Saturday, he received his second booking of the season for leaving his technical area. This, it turns out, is another part of the vast conspiracy against Arsenal. Yes, Arteta accepted, he left his technical area (44 times before being booked, according to the former referee Graham Scott), but other managers do it too. “There are managers who have the record in the league, 36 times in 10 minutes [they] leave the touchline – no yellows,” he said. “I am clipping all of that … so if somebody comes to me I can say: ‘I am not in the record yet.’ Somebody else has the record so let’s see. Then it’s 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for the managers.” Continue reading...

item.title: Troops neutralize suspected bandits in Kogi shootout
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Sector 3, Joint Task Force Operation Whirl Stroke have neutralized a suspected bandit following an intelligence-led ambush along the Adankolo–Apata Road in Kogi State. The operation, conducted on Saturday 31 October 2026, followed credible intelligence on the movement of suspected terrorists around communities in Kabba-Bunu and Lokoja Local Government Areas of the state. Spokesman of the Sector, Captain Ahmad Zubairu who made this known, said the troops acting on the intelligence, troops laid ambush at suspected bandits’ supply route. “The troops subsequently made contact with the suspected criminals who were subdued and forced to flee. “At about 9pm on the same day during exploitation, troops received information regarding the discovery of suspected bandits’ bodies towards Adankolo Forest. “On arrival at the location, troops found corpses of the two suspected bandits and recovered one locally made pistol, one cartridge and one empty case of 7.62mm special ammunition. “The Force Commander, Joint Task Force Operation Whirl Stroke and General Officer Commanding 5 Division, Nigerian Army, Major General Moses Gara, commended the troops for their gallantry and successful execution of the operation. “He urged members of the public to continue supporting security agencies by providing timely and credible information on suspicious activities, stressing that security remains everybody’s responsibility. “The Force Commander reiterated the commitment of Operation Whirl Stroke to sustaining intelligence-led operations aimed at protecting lives and property across its Area of Responsibility.” The post Troops neutralize suspected bandits in Kogi shootout appeared first on Vanguard News .

Produced by The Elements, the track fuses sharp Afropop delivery with a seamless multilingual switch between English and French. The video leans into a brilliant, high-fashion pop-art universe built around currency motifs, retro magazine layouts, and custom toy-box packaging. Ayra shifts effortlessly through striking visual aesthetics, from a pink mini-dress with cowrie shell details to a rich blue halter top set against vibrant red hair and statement face detailing, making it a complete visual treat. “Commando” – Joshua Baraka featuring Tiwa Savage East meets West in the smoothest fashion as Ugandan singer Joshua Baraka links up with Afrobeats royalty Tiwa Savage for “Commando”, a standout cut from the Recess II project. Joshua Baraka’s soulful R&B-infused delivery pairs wonderfully with Tiwa’s signature vocal versatility, creating a cozy, late-night vibe that is impossible to shake off. “TAFI” – TY Bello featuring Tomi Favored For those looking to slow things down and lean into a deep, meditative space, TY Bello and Tomi Favored deliver an incredible worship experience with “TAFI (Pass Over)”. It is an immersive, beautifully captured session that invites complete reflection and peace. “Ndewo” – Phyno featuring Wande Coal Penthauze boss Phyno joins forces with the legendary Wande Coal for “Ndewo”, a massive collaboration off Phyno’s project Let That Sink In (LTSI). item.title: Iran says US tone has ‘changed’ as Washington seeks negotiations
item.description: Iran on Saturday said the tone of the United States had “completely changed” as Washington seeks to restart negotiations with the Islamic republic. While the US and Israel have upped their threats to order fresh strikes, Vice President JD Vance also sent a letter to Iranian officials in recent days in a bid to revive talks. “I read the letter. I haven’t yet responded. Their tone has completely changed,” Mohsen Rezaei, the head of Iran’s supreme national security council, said in a video broadcast on Iranian television. He said the change in tone was “a good sign” and showed Iran had “consolidated its victory”. Rezaei said he had not responded to the letter and would not comment further on its contents. His comments came as indirect mediation via Qatar continued, though Iranian officials said earlier on Saturday that they had no plans to meet with US officials. The post Iran says US tone has ‘changed’ as Washington seeks negotiations appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Miyetti Allah backs Tinubu’s re-election, cites livestock ministry
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The National President of the Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria (MACBAN), Baba Othman Ngelzarma, has declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, citing the establishment of the Federal Ministry of Livestock Development as a major step towards addressing decades of neglect of the livestock sector. Ngelzarma said pastoralists, cattle breeders and other livestock stakeholders across the country were prepared to support Tinubu for a second term in appreciation of his administration’s recognition of the economic importance of the sector. He spoke at a rally organised in Kaduna by the Fulbe APC Forum and Tinubu Yeso-Yeso Political Forum (TYPF), in collaboration with the Coalition of Pastoralists and Traders Associations and the Amalgamated Union of Livestock Dealers, Butchers and other stakeholders. The rally, held under the theme, “United for Inclusion, Representation and Prosperity,” attracted Fulani organisations, pastoralists, cattle breeders, livestock dealers, butchers, processors and political stakeholders from different parts of the country. Ngelzarma said the creation of the livestock ministry in July 2024 had fulfilled a longstanding demand by pastoralists and livestock operators, who had campaigned for a dedicated government institution to address challenges in the industry for several decades. “We are here today to extend our appreciation and support to the administration of President Tinubu. “The creation of the livestock ministry is something we have been advocating for and looking forward to for decades,” he said. He noted that the initiative had also encouraged some state governments to establish similar institutions to coordinate livestock development, describing it as an opportunity to address longstanding challenges confronting pastoralists and other operators in the industry. The Minister of Livestock Development, Idi Mukhtar Maiha, urged pastoralists, livestock farmers and other stakeholders to take advantage of the ministry’s programmes to improve productivity, expand their businesses and enhance their livelihoods. Maiha identified inadequate veterinary services, limited access to pasture and water, high feed costs, poor market infrastructure and low productivity as some of the factors that had hindered the growth of Nigeria’s livestock industry over the years. He said Nigeria had an estimated 58 million cattle, 124 million goats, 70 million sheep, 9.3 million pigs, 3.2 million donkeys, 700,000 camels and 300 million birds, describing the figures as enormous economic opportunities that could be harnessed through deliberate investments and improved management. The minister disclosed that seven veterinary hospitals had been completed and equipped under a World Bank-supported programme, while additional facilities were at various stages of completion. He said the Federal Government planned to expand veterinary services across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Ter

item.content:encoded: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The National President of the Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria (MACBAN), Baba Othman Ngelzarma, has declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, citing the establishment of the Federal Ministry of Livestock Development as a major step towards addressing decades of neglect of the livestock sector. Ngelzarma said pastoralists, cattle breeders and other livestock stakeholders across the country were prepared to support Tinubu for a second term in appreciation of his administration’s recognition of the economic importance of the sector. He spoke at a rally organised in Kaduna by the Fulbe APC Forum and Tinubu Yeso-Yeso Political Forum (TYPF), in collaboration with the Coalition of Pastoralists and Traders Associations and the Amalgamated Union of Livestock Dealers, Butchers and other stakeholders. The rally, held under the theme, “United for Inclusion, Representation and Prosperity,” attracted Fulani organisations, pastoralists, cattle breeders, livestock dealers, butchers, processors and political stakeholders from different parts of the country. Ngelzarma said the creation of the livestock ministry in July 2024 had fulfilled a longstanding demand by pastoralists and livestock operators, who had campaigned for a dedicated government institution to address challenges in the industry for several decades. “We are here today to extend our appreciation and support to the administration of President Tinubu. “The creation of the livestock ministry is something we have been advocating for and looking forward to for decades,” he said. He noted that the initiative had also encouraged some state governments to establish similar institutions to coordinate livestock development, describing it as an opportunity to address longstanding challenges confronting pastoralists and other operators in the industry. The Minister of Livestock Development, Idi Mukhtar Maiha, urged pastoralists, livestock farmers and other stakeholders to take advantage of the ministry’s programmes to improve productivity, expand their businesses and enhance their livelihoods. Maiha identified inadequate veterinary services, limited access to pasture and water, high feed costs, poor market infrastructure and low productivity as some of the factors that had hindered the growth of Nigeria’s livestock industry over the years. He said Nigeria had an estimated 58 million cattle, 124 million goats, 70 million sheep, 9.3 million pigs, 3.2 million donkeys, 700,000 camels and 300 million birds, describing the figures as enormous economic opportunities that could be harnessed through deliberate investments and improved management. The minister disclosed that seven veterinary hospitals had been completed and equipped under a World Bank-supported programme, while additional facilities were at various stages of completion. He said the Federal Government planned to expand veterinary services across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, with primary veterinary facilities also envisaged for the 774 local government areas. Maiha challenged livestock associations to work with the ministry and state governments within three months to identify the challenges confronting their members and develop practical proposals for investment and improved service delivery. He said the government was also working to strengthen Nigeria’s participation in regional and international livestock trade through improved animal health standards, traceability systems and market infrastructure. On the recurring tensions between farmers and pastoralists, the minister stressed the need for peaceful coexistence, dialogue and responsible management of land and water resources, noting that sustainable livestock development depended on harmonious relationships between farming and pastoral communities. He also urged young Nigerians to embrace livestock production as a viable business capable of generating employment and wealth, rather than viewing it merely as a traditional occupation. In his remarks, Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani, represented by the Commissioner for Agriculture, Murtala Dabo, said the state government was complementing the Federal Government’s initiative through investments in livestock infrastructure and services. Dabo disclosed that Kaduna State’s budgetary allocation to livestock development had increased from N1.48 billion in 2023 to more than N100 billion in 2026. He said the state government had provided solar-powered water facilities in pastoralist communities, expanded livestock vaccination programmes and introduced artificial insemination services to improve animal productivity. According to him, improved feeding and breeding practices had increased milk production among some cattle from about 1.5 litres to between three and four litres. He added that the government was also upgrading slaughter facilities and improving infrastructure across the livestock value chain to boost production, processing and marketing. item.title: Gov. Lawal presents staff of office, vehicles to 19 Zamfara emirs
item.description: Governor Dauda Lawal has presented staff of office and official vehicles to 19 emirs in Zamfara State. The coronation and presentation ceremony took place at the Trade Fair Complex in Gusau, the state capital. Dignitaries in attendance included His Eminence the Sultan of Sokoto, the Etsu Nupe, and the Emir of Gwandu. After their oaths of office, Governor Lawal presented staff of office to 11 first-class emirs and eight second-class emirs. Each newly coronated emir also received a GAC Ultra SUV (2025/2026 model), a Mikano ZNA Hilux vehicle and an EV Antique Model car (DDP). The vehicles are intended to support their travels and help them engage more closely with their communities. In his remarks, Governor Lawal said the ceremony reflected his administration’s recognition of the traditional institution as an enduring part of society and an important partner in promoting peace, stability and development. He noted that the ceremony also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to giving traditional rulers the recognition and institutional support they need to carry out their responsibilities effectively. He said, “The staff of office being presented today signifies the authority entrusted to you by the State. “It also represents a responsibility to govern your respective domains with fairness, wisdom, integrity, and compassion. “I expect every emir to carry out their responsibilities without discrimination, uphold justice, and ensure that the traditional institution remains accessible to all members of the community. “Our people must find guidance, fairness, and reassurance in their traditional rulers. “Recognising the importance of royal palaces as centres of traditional authority and community engagement, I reaffirm our commitment to completing the reconstruction and rehabilitation of the remaining royal palaces. “This is part of our broader effort to strengthen these institutions and improve the conditions in which traditional rulers carry out their responsibilities. “We are also providing official vehicles to the 19 emirs. These include GAC ULTRA SUVs (2025/2026 models), MIKANO ZNA HILUX vehicles, and EV ANTIQUE MODEL cars (DDP). “This provision is intended to facilitate travel across your respective emirates, encourage closer engagement with your communities, and improve coordination with government institutions. “I expect these vehicles to be properly maintained and used responsibly in support of your official duties.” The governor also urged the royal fathers to build a productive partnership between their emirates and the state government. Earlier, the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Sa’ad Abubakar, urged the newly coronated emirs to remain fully loyal to the authority. He also encouraged them to respect and uphold the dignity of the traditional institution as they discharge their duties. The post Gov. Lawal presents staff of office, vehicles to 19 Zamfara emirs appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Sowore reacts as Ekiti police arrest 11 over attack
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The Ekiti State Police Command has arrested 11 suspects over the attack on African Action Congress (AAC) presidential aspirant, Omoyele Sowore, and members of his team at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti, the state capital. In a statement on Saturday, the command’s Public Relations Officer, Abutu Sunday, said operatives of the Rapid Response Squad arrested the suspects at their hideouts in the Atikankan area of the town at about 10pm on Friday, following a tip-off. It partly reads, “The Ekiti State Police Command has arrested eleven (11) suspects in connection with the alleged attack on Mr Omoyele Sowore, an African Action Congress (AAC) presidential aspirant, and other persons at Tawakalitu Restaurant, Dalimore Area of Ado-Ekiti. “The suspects are Joseph Tayo ’32yrs’, Olatunji Abayomi ’41yrs’, Isaac Amba ’22yrs’, Kehinde Ajigbana ’18yrs’, Tosin David ’18yrs’, Solomon Iyanu ’18yrs’, Ogunsola Ayomide ’21yrs’, Ojo Ayodeji ’22yrs’, Kayode Dada ’32yrs’, Segun Olatunji ’28yrs’ and Salami Emmanuel ’53yrs’. “Items recovered include two walkie-talkies, substances suspected to be Indian hemp and Colorado, two Indian hemp crushers, one pack of Rizla, seven ATM cards, thirteen mobile phones, two vehicle keys, one flash drive, one 5G MTN Wi-Fi device, identity cards, eight international passports, three complimentary cards, two suspected criminal charms, one gas lighter and ₦250.” The police said investigations were ongoing to establish the individual roles of the suspects and determine their possible connections with the attack. The Commissioner of Police, Falade Michael, assured residents that everyone found culpable would be brought to justice. The statement quoted him as saying that the command “will leave no stone unturned in ensuring that all those found culpable are brought to justice.” Reacting to the arrests, Sowore demanded that the alleged masterminds and sponsors of the attack be identified and brought to justice, insisting that the incident was a coordinated assault and not an ordinary altercation. The presidential candidate made the demand in a post on X on Saturday, describing the arrests as an admission that the incident was a violent attack. He also alleged that some of the attackers were associated with the City Boys group and called for investigations into possible links between the incident and officials of the state government. Sowore urged the Commissioner of Police, Falade Adegoroye Michael, and the Department of State Services to preserve and release CCTV footage from the scene to help identify those involved. “Arresting 11 suspects is not enough if those who planned, financed, coordinated and facilitated the attack remain untouched,” he wrote. He also demanded an explanation from the police over their initial description of the incident as an altercation. The post Sowore reacts as Ekiti police arrest 11 over attack appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: ‘Don’t be deceived, vote for Tinubu’ – South-East govs tell Igbo
item.description: Governors of Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu and Imo States have urged the people not to be deceived by political distractions but to vote massively for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election. The governors made the call on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) Women Mega Rally and Empowerment Programme for the South-East, held at Okpara Square, Enugu. The governors are Prof. Charles Soludo of Anambra, Francis Nwifuru of Ebonyi, Dr Peter Mbah of Enugu and Sen. Hope Uzodimma of Imo. Speaking, Mbah urged the people of the South-East to support Tinubu’s re-election bid to enable him to consolidate the gains of his administration’s economic reforms. He attributed ongoing development projects, including the construction of primary healthcare centres, to the Federal Government’s economic reforms. The governor urged women to support Tinubu and APC candidates in the Jan. 16, 2027, and subsequent elections. “A good sailor does not abandon his ship mid-sea because of challenges. We must finish the journey we all started together,” he said. Mbah described South Easterners as strategic people who had established businesses and relationships beyond the zone, urging them to participate actively in the political process. Speaking on the empowerment programme targeting 5,000 women across the South-East, Mbah said the initiative followed the empowerment of more than 2,000 women in Enugu within 48 hours. He said the beneficiaries received cash support, assistance with hospital bills and tools to enable them to generate income. According to him, the programme is designed to make women wealth creators rather than perpetual beneficiaries of financial assistance. “When you empower a woman, you strengthen the family. When you empower a woman, you build a strong community,” he said. He urged the beneficiaries to make effective use of the empowerment tools and extend the benefits to their families and communities. Uzodimma Also speaking, Uzodimma described the rally as historic and commended the First Lady, Sen. Oluremi Tinubu, for empowering women across the South-East. He reiterated the commitment of the region to supporting Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. He explained that Igbos had experienced marginalisation for over 60 years but were beginning to witness a new era of political inclusion and development under Tinubu. He commended the president for expanding the scope of infrastructural and economic development in the South-East. “We are now seeing good roads, electricity, health reforms as well as educational reforms in the country. item.content:encoded: Governors of Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu and Imo States have urged the people not to be deceived by political distractions but to vote massively for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election. The governors made the call on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) Women Mega Rally and Empowerment Programme for the South-East, held at Okpara Square, Enugu. The governors are Prof. Charles Soludo of Anambra, Francis Nwifuru of Ebonyi, Dr Peter Mbah of Enugu and Sen. Hope Uzodimma of Imo. Speaking, Mbah urged the people of the South-East to support Tinubu’s re-election bid to enable him to consolidate the gains of his administration’s economic reforms. He attributed ongoing development projects, including the construction of primary healthcare centres, to the Federal Government’s economic reforms. The governor urged women to support Tinubu and APC candidates in the Jan. 16, 2027, and subsequent elections. “A good sailor does not abandon his ship mid-sea because of challenges. We must finish the journey we all started together,” he said. Mbah described South Easterners as strategic people who had established businesses and relationships beyond the zone, urging them to participate actively in the political process. Speaking on the empowerment programme targeting 5,000 women across the South-East, Mbah said the initiative followed the empowerment of more than 2,000 women in Enugu within 48 hours. He said the beneficiaries received cash support, assistance with hospital bills and tools to enable them to generate income. According to him, the programme is designed to make women wealth creators rather than perpetual beneficiaries of financial assistance. “When you empower a woman, you strengthen the family. When you empower a woman, you build a strong community,” he said. He urged the beneficiaries to make effective use of the empowerment tools and extend the benefits to their families and communities. Uzodimma Also speaking, Uzodimma described the rally as historic and commended the First Lady, Sen. Oluremi Tinubu, for empowering women across the South-East. He reiterated the commitment of the region to supporting Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. He explained that Igbos had experienced marginalisation for over 60 years but were beginning to witness a new era of political inclusion and development under Tinubu. He commended the president for expanding the scope of infrastructural and economic development in the South-East. “We are now seeing good roads, electricity, health reforms as well as educational reforms in the country. A winning team must not be changed,” he said. The governor urged the electorate to sustain the current development trajectory, saying the Federal Government’s economic reforms had increased resources available to states for development. “We have more money to build Okigwe to Owerri, Umuahia to Owerri, Orlu to Owerri and Owerri to Port Harcourt roads,” he said. Uzodimma added that the improved financial position of the state had enabled his administration to pay salaries and pensions consistently, including 13th-month salaries for workers. In his remarks, Nwifuru commended the skills acquisition and empowerment initiatives of the APC-led administration, urging South-East women to vote massively for the party. He described the APC as the only political party with a clear and identifiable manifesto capable of sustaining the country’s development. The governor dismissed suggestions of his involvement in any political coalition, stressing that his loyalty remained with the APC. He urged supporters to vote for APC candidates at all levels in the January 2027 elections and subsequent polls. Soludo Similarly, Soludo, represented by his Deputy, Dr Gilbert Ibezim, said the South-East had a responsibility to support Tinubu’s re-election in appreciation of his administration’s achievements. He said the region stood to benefit more from continued collaboration with the Federal Government. Also speaking, the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Mr Benjamin Kalu, urged Igbos to embrace political inclusion by supporting Tinubu’s re-election. Kalu said the Igbo had not produced a president of Nigeria in the past 60 years, stressing the need for the region to strengthen its political alliances. He recalled that Tinubu, while serving as governor of Lagos State, maintained cordial relationships with Igbos and included them in his cabinet. He commended the Tinubu administration for establishing the South East Development Commission (SEDC). He described it as a major step towards addressing the region’s developmental challenges. item.title: Police repel bandits’ attack on Kebbi community
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Police Command has said that it is aware of the security incident in Ribah, Zuru Local Government Area, on 30th October 2026, when suspected bandits launched two successive attacks on the community. Police image maker, in a statement on Saturday, revealed that the first incident occurred at about 7:25 pm, when the assailants attempted to block Rambo Junction along the Ribah–Dirin Daji Road under Zuru emirate, as their attempt was promptly foiled by the joint security forces comprising the police, military and local vigilante group, who engaged them in a gun duel and dispersed them. The statement added that the attackers later regrouped and returned, shooting sporadically from different directions within the town. However, during the ensuing exchange, one Hassan Boder, aged 47, a security guard at a newly constructed filling station along Ribah–Kanya Road, was fatally hit by a bullet. Upon receipt of a distress call, the joint security team swiftly mobilised, engaged the attackers and successfully repelled them. Usman explained that security operations have since been intensified, with aggressive patrols ongoing to dominate the area and efforts underway to track down and apprehend the perpetrators. “Yes, we are aware of the attack and we have repelled it by forcing the terrorists to retreat due to superior firepower. The combined security forces have dominated the area to prevent further attacks on the communities,” he said. The post Police repel bandits’ attack on Kebbi community appeared first on Vanguard News .

Usman explained that security operations have since been intensified, with aggressive patrols ongoing to dominate the area and efforts underway to track down and apprehend the perpetrators. “Yes, we are aware of the attack and we have repelled it by forcing the terrorists to retreat due to superior firepower. The combined security forces have dominated the area to prevent further attacks on the communities,” he said. The post Police repel bandits’ attack on Kebbi community appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Clashes break out as hundreds of thousands protest in France
item.description: Police fired tear gas and clashed with protesters in Paris and elsewhere on Saturday as hundreds of thousands marched across France against soaring living costs and police violence, with some demonstrators dressed as clowns and witches for Halloween. While the third consecutive weekend of nationwide protests was largely peaceful, tensions erupted in several cities later Saturday. After a march on the outskirts of Paris in bright sunshine, clashes broke out between police and some demonstrators as the procession reached its final destination. Dozens of masked people dressed in black used hammers to pry up paving stones and hurl them at police. At least one incendiary device was also thrown at security forces. Police responded with tear gas and several baton charges. “A hard core of several hundred rioters” at the rear of the march attacked police with projectiles, including a Molotov cocktail, the police prefecture said. Officers were seeking “to restore public order”, it added. In Lyon, France’s third-largest city, people threw projectiles at police, prompting officers to fire tear gas, according to a journalist at the scene. In the southern city of Toulouse, police used water cannon against an unauthorised protest that drew several thousand people, mostly young demonstrators. – ‘Dressed up as angry citizen’ – Earlier Saturday, thousands of people, some wearing costumes ranging from Spider-Man to Frankenstein, walked through eastern Paris as a helicopter circled overhead. Placards read: “No need for tear gas to make our future look bleak” and “Dressed up as an angry citizen for Halloween.” A protester wearing a Marie-Antoinette costume (L) holds a placard reading “Give them brioche” flanked by a protester dressed as a wizard holding a placard reading “A potion for the revolution” during a demonstration in Lyon, central-eastern France on October 31, 2026, part of nationwide demonstrations over the rising cost of living and inequality organised by Yellow Vest movement, labour unions and high school and university students. “Exceptional” security deployment with 70,000 police officers and gendarmes mobilized and an alarmist tone: for Act III of the protests against the high cost of living, right in the middle of Halloween festivities, the authorities fear a repeat of the October 17 nightmare. France has been rocked by widespread anger over the rising cost of living and inequality. (Photo by JEFF PACHOUD / AFP) “We say no to the cost of living, no to the far right, yes to high school students’ demands, yes to giving citizens a voice,” said Camille Guerin, 31, a demonstrator in the western city of Nantes. item.content:encoded: Police fired tear gas and clashed with protesters in Paris and elsewhere on Saturday as hundreds of thousands marched across France against soaring living costs and police violence, with some demonstrators dressed as clowns and witches for Halloween. While the third consecutive weekend of nationwide protests was largely peaceful, tensions erupted in several cities later Saturday. After a march on the outskirts of Paris in bright sunshine, clashes broke out between police and some demonstrators as the procession reached its final destination. Dozens of masked people dressed in black used hammers to pry up paving stones and hurl them at police. At least one incendiary device was also thrown at security forces. Police responded with tear gas and several baton charges. “A hard core of several hundred rioters” at the rear of the march attacked police with projectiles, including a Molotov cocktail, the police prefecture said. Officers were seeking “to restore public order”, it added. In Lyon, France’s third-largest city, people threw projectiles at police, prompting officers to fire tear gas, according to a journalist at the scene. In the southern city of Toulouse, police used water cannon against an unauthorised protest that drew several thousand people, mostly young demonstrators. – ‘Dressed up as angry citizen’ – Earlier Saturday, thousands of people, some wearing costumes ranging from Spider-Man to Frankenstein, walked through eastern Paris as a helicopter circled overhead. Placards read: “No need for tear gas to make our future look bleak” and “Dressed up as an angry citizen for Halloween.” A protester wearing a Marie-Antoinette costume (L) holds a placard reading “Give them brioche” flanked by a protester dressed as a wizard holding a placard reading “A potion for the revolution” during a demonstration in Lyon, central-eastern France on October 31, 2026, part of nationwide demonstrations over the rising cost of living and inequality organised by Yellow Vest movement, labour unions and high school and university students. “Exceptional” security deployment with 70,000 police officers and gendarmes mobilized and an alarmist tone: for Act III of the protests against the high cost of living, right in the middle of Halloween festivities, the authorities fear a repeat of the October 17 nightmare. France has been rocked by widespread anger over the rising cost of living and inequality. (Photo by JEFF PACHOUD / AFP) “We say no to the cost of living, no to the far right, yes to high school students’ demands, yes to giving citizens a voice,” said Camille Guerin, 31, a demonstrator in the western city of Nantes. Authorities said that some 320,000 people rallied across France including 70,000 in Paris. According to youth organisations, nearly half a million people demonstrated across the country, including 200,000 in Paris. An aide to Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on Friday that police had prepared for street violence on a scale “comparable” to the unrest two weeks ago, when shops were looted and public buildings set ablaze. Between 400 and 800 hard-left activists were expected in Paris, said an informed source. – Elections looming – The demonstrations come in a febrile political climate, with presidential elections less than six months away and far-right leader Marine Le Pen topping opinion polls. The protest movement, bringing together Yellow Vest activists, trade unions, and high school and university students, initially focused on the rising cost of living, inequality, and deteriorating learning conditions. Following a security clampdown and serious injuries to some protesters, the movement broadened its demands to include greater protection of civil liberties and the right to protest. Similar youth-led demonstrations have been seen across Europe in recent weeks. Thousands of young Germans took to the streets nationwide on Saturday. In the northern French city of Lille, 47-year-old Aurelie Herrmann danced at the protest. “I dance because on television they only show damage and destruction, whereas you can perfectly well demonstrate in good spirits,” she said. “Struggle is classy, it needs to come back into fashion.” – New school blockades – Student protesters complained the police did not authorise a march through the centre of the French capital and vowed to stage new blockades of high schools and universities next week. “Starting this Tuesday, we will blockade our universities and high schools, and we will do so again on Thursday before joining the demonstration on November 5 called by workers and trade unions,” said Sabrine Kharbach, spokeswoman for the Union Etudiante (Student Union). Ahead of the protests, some shopkeepers barricaded their businesses. In eastern Paris, Wael Boubaker, a cafe employee, covered a storefront with plywood panels. “Everyone is staying home. No one is going to come and buy anything,” Boubaker said. Hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon, who accused Macron’s government of “taking an increasingly authoritarian turn”, joined the march in Paris. With the eurozone’s second-largest economy on the brink of recession and under pressure to rein in its debt, the government has limited scope to appease protesters through additional spending. Nunez said authorities had detected social media calls for Halloween gatherings on Saturday evening that urged protesters to spark a “revolution”. item.title: US yet to decide on new Iran strikes, says Rubio
item.description: US President Donald Trump has not made a decision about fresh strikes on Iran amid stalled peace talks, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday. “We can achieve military objectives if we seek to,” Rubio told a press conference in Atlanta, Georgia, where he was hosting G20 foreign ministers for a two-day meeting. But Rubio added that Trump “hasn’t made a decision” on further military action, amid reports that the US leader could attack after key midterm elections on Tuesday. “I have no announcement in that regard with you today, and nor do we take any of it lightly,” Rubio said. While he slammed Tehran for “actively and openly” targeting commercial vessels for attack, Rubio also expressed Trump’s preference for a diplomatic solution to end war with Iran. But he did not commit to a timeline for talks. “I’m not going to characterize neither the progress on those talks nor any timeframe on it, other than to tell you that if there is a diplomatic solution, we would be open to it,” Rubio said. Iran’s supreme leader on Saturday warned the United States and Israel against launching new attacks, following threats to resume strikes after crucial elections. Trump earlier warned of the potential for fresh military action after US midterms, saying previously that he was weighing up whether to “finish them off.” But any further attack would spark concern among US allies. On Thursday, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas told AFP: “We are calling for a diplomatic solution, and really, escalation does not benefit anyone.” AFP The post US yet to decide on new Iran strikes, says Rubio appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: Michael Carrick is now a little more pre-doomed, pre-sacked, but is miles away from being the actual story On and on and on. And then on just a little bit more it would seem. Manchester United: always crashing in the same Carrick. The obvious question after this 2-0 defeat to Chelsea is how much longer United will continue to lose games under the current manager, as opposed to losing games under the next one. But it is also a mark of the dysfunction of this club, its ambient levels of sadness, that this matters so little. Continue reading...

item.title: Man City Stunned In 0-1 Home Loss To Brighton
item.description: Manchester City suffered a second straight Premier League defeat at the hands of Brighton with a 1-0 win as the Seagulls went close within two points of the leaders on Saturday. Third-placed Brighton ended their wait for a first-ever away win against City on their 18th attempt to bolster dreams of challenging for the title. The Seagulls have never won a major trophy but have already beaten champions Arsenal convincingly this season to show their title credentials. Fabian Hurzeler’s men got revenge for defeat to City on penalties in the League Cup on Wednesday. Brighton’s French midfielder Georginio Rutter is put under pressure by Manchester City’s Portuguese midfielder Matheus Nunes (L) and Manchester City’s English midfielder #05 Elliot Anderson (R) during the English Premier League football match between Manchester City and Brighton and Hove Albion at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) Hurzeler felt aggrieved at that result after his side twice led at the Etihad and this time held on after Yasin Ayari slotted them into an 11th-minute lead. Bart Verbruggen was inspired in the Brighton goal to see off a City onslaught after half-time. Brighton’s German head coach Fabian Hurzeler reacts after the English Premier League football match between Manchester City and Brighton and Hove Albion at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) / But the visitors were well worthy of a famous win and could also have added to their lead when Jack Hinshelwood hit the side netting late on. City won their opening seven league games as Enzo Maresca made a flawless start to the daunting task of succeeding Pep Guardiola. Manchester City’s Norwegian striker Erling Haaland reacts following the English Premier League football match between Manchester City and Brighton and Hove Albion at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) However, the 10-time English champions know their results on the field may count for little this season unless they can successfully overturn a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules. City have appealed, but if that ruling is upheld, they are likely to face a severe points penalty and possible relegation from the English top-flight. Defeat for Maresca’s men means Arsenal can go top of the table if they avoid losing at Liverpool on Sunday. Man Utd Self-Implode Meanwhile, City’s neighbours Manchester United recorded their nine-game winless run, their longest without victory for 38 years, after a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea. The Red Devils were left to regret not taking advantage of a series of first-half chances to take the lead before they imploded in the second period. The Red Devils were left to regret not taking advantage of a series of first-half chances to take the lead before they imploded in the second period. Morgan Rogers was allowed to run straight through the heart of the United defence to open the scoring. Lisandro Martinez then did his under-pressure manager no favours with two quickfire yellow cards, the second of which also conceded a penalty. Cole Palmer converted from the spot to lift Chelsea into the top four. “The two halves of football couldn’t probably be further apart,” said Carrick, who added he expects to be in charge for Tuesday’s Champions League tie against Roma. “We looked in a good place going into half-time and then found a way of unravelling it second half.” Only Nottingham Forest’s 2-0 defeat at Brentford ensured United did not drop into the bottom three. Nikola Milenkovic’s own goal and Igor Thiago’s strike took the Bees up to sixth. Bournemouth extended their fine form with a 2-0 win over Leeds thanks to goals from Evanilson and Amine Adli. Sunderland remain rooted to the foot of the table after a 3-1 defeat at Coventry. Hull and Ipswich played out a 2-2 draw. item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Okogba
item.content:encoded: Brighton inflicted a second straight Premier League defeat on Manchester City with a 1-0 win to close within two points of the leaders on Saturday, while Manchester United slumped to another damaging defeat for Michael Carrick at Chelsea. Third-placed Brighton ended their wait for a first ever away win against City at the 18th attempt to bolster dreams of challenging for the title. The Seagulls have never won a major trophy but have already beaten champions Arsenal convincingly this season to show their title credentials. Fabian Hurzeler’s men got revenge for defeat to City on penalties in the League Cup on Wednesday. Hurzeler felt aggrieved at that result after his side twice led at the Etihad and this time held on after Yasin Ayari slotted them into an 11th-minute lead. Bart Verbruggen was inspired in the Brighton goal to see off a City onslaught after half-time. But the visitors were well worthy of a famous win and could also have added to their lead when Jack Hinshelwood hit the side-netting late on. Players celebrate following the English Premier League football match between Manchester City and Brighton and Hove Albion at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) City won their opening seven league games as Enzo Maresca made a flawless start to the daunting task of succeeding Pep Guardiola. However, the 10-time English champions know their results on the field may count for little this season unless they can successfully overturn a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules. City have appealed, but if that ruling is upheld they are likely to face a severe points penalty and possible relegation from the English top-flight. Defeat for Maresca’s men means Arsenal can go top of the table if they avoid losing at Liverpool on Sunday. – Man Utd self-implode – Manchester United’s nine-game winless run is their longest without victory for 38 years after a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea. The Red Devils were left to regret not taking advantage of a series of first half chances to take the lead before they imploded in the second period. Morgan Rogers was allowed to run straight through the heart of the United defence to open the scoring. Lisandro Martinez then did his under-pressure manager no favours with two quickfire yellow cards, the second of which also conceded a penalty. Chelsea’s English midfielder #10 Cole Palmer (L) vies with Manchester United’s Brazilian striker #10 Matheus Cunha (R) during the English Premier League football match between Chelsea and Manchester United at Stamford Bridge in London on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Glyn KIRK / AFP) Cole Palmer converted from the spot to lift Chelsea into the top four. “The two halves of football couldn’t probably be further apart,” said Carrick, who added he expects to be in charge for Tuesday’s Champions League tie against Roma. “We looked in a good place going into half-time and then found a way of unravelling it second half.” Only Nottingham Forest’s 2-0 defeat at Brentford ensured United did not drop into the bottom three. Nikola Milenkovic’s own goal and Igor Thiago’s strike took the Bees up to sixth. Bournemouth extended their fine form with a 2-0 win over Leeds thanks to goals from Evanilson and Amine Adli. Sunderland remain rooted to the foot of the table after a 3-1 defeat at Coventry. Hull and Ipswich played out a 2-2 draw. kca/nf The post EPL: Brighton stun Man City, 10-man Man Utd beaten by Chelsea appeared first on Vanguard News .
